project.name: a9loader
project.description: A mod loader for A-Train 9 v5: a Rust workspace whose version.dll proxy applies expect-verified, journaled memory effects inside the running game process, keeping the game directory vanilla. Contains the shared format codecs (pack cipher, LZSS, family-A/B containers, i.dat, csvp, savegame members), the mod model, the loader DLL, and the a9ml authoring/diagnostics CLI. Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

nodes.name: buildid.rs
nodes.summary: Reads the game exe's PE VERSIONINFO straight from the file bytes (no Win32 API, so no loader-lock hazard) and yields the canonical build id such as "5.00.5634" that gates memory effects.

nodes.name: builds.rs
nodes.summary: The per-build anchor address book (builds.toml): maps named anchors to an RVA plus the expected original bytes the loader must verify before any anchored write.

nodes.name: config.rs
nodes.summary: Parses a9loader.toml (log level, mods dir, ordering, serving modes, workspace sizing, diagnostic probes) leniently-but-loudly: a missing file is defaults, a broken or unknown key is a warning, never a failed boot.

nodes.name: dirindex.rs
nodes.summary: The per-build dir-to-pack index (dirindex.toml) that resolves `host = "auto"` assets: exact name, then dir, then longest prefix, refusing loudly on ambiguity instead of guessing a pack.

nodes.name: hex.rs
nodes.summary: Hex-string helpers for manifest `data`/`expect` fields and address-book expects, accepting both the human comma form and compact hex, case-insensitive.

nodes.name: lib.rs
nodes.summary: Crate root of a9-mod: declares the module tree of the shared mod model and defines ModError, the io/parse/invalid error enum used across the crate.

nodes.name: new

nodes.name: tuple

nodes.name: from_exe_bytes

nodes.name: embedded

nodes.name: anchor
nodes.summary: Looks up a named anchor in this build's anchor map.

nodes.name: parse

nodes.name: embedded_book
nodes.summary: Parses the embedded address book — used by the loader at boot and by tests to keep the shipped book valid.

nodes.name: LogLevel

nodes.name: read

nodes.name: DirIndex

nodes.name: BuildIndex

nodes.name: embedded
nodes.summary: Returns the dirindex.toml shipped in the repository via include_str!.

nodes.name: embedded_index

nodes.name: validate
nodes.summary: Dispatches the per-section checks in schema order, threading the shared patch/hook target-key set.

nodes.name: validate_identity
nodes.summary: Enforces the mod id's lowercase-slug shape.

nodes.name: validate_lists
nodes.summary: Rejects empty entries in the game_builds/supplies/requires/conflicts lists.

nodes.name: validate_patches
nodes.summary: Checks [[patch]] entries for unique shared target keys, non-empty valid hex data and the raw-target expect requirement.

nodes.summary: Checks [[hook]] entries for unique shared target keys and the per-handler parameter shapes (train_list needs a list, nop takes none).

nodes.summary: Checks [[pack]] sections: lowercase-slug pack name, one section per pack, not csvp, at least one entry, unique entry names and a payload file each.

nodes.name: validate_assets
nodes.summary: Checks [[asset]] sections: exactly one of single-file or folder form, non-empty names, no NULs, unique names and a valid host.

nodes.name: validate_asset_host
nodes.summary: Checks an asset's host is "auto" or a family-A opaque pack the loader can append to (vp/tp/mcp/ep/cp).

nodes.name: validate_mod_rel_path

nodes.name: ResolveConfig
nodes.summary: The resolver's inputs: explicit sequence, per-mod priority overrides, disabled ids and the allow-conflicts flag.

nodes.name: Skip
nodes.summary: A mod skipped by the resolver, with its index, id and human-readable reason.

nodes.name: Overlap

nodes.name: effect_refused
nodes.summary: True when a mod's effect on a key lost an overlap to an earlier mod.

nodes.name: resolve
nodes.summary: The planner entry point: runs base order, sequence, disabled, requires fixpoint, conflicts and overlap collection in turn.

nodes.name: apply_sequence
nodes.summary: Pulls explicitly sequenced ids to the front in listed order, leaving the rest in base order behind them.

nodes.name: apply_disabled
nodes.summary: Drops config-disabled mods, recording each as a skip.

nodes.name: apply_requires_fixpoint
nodes.summary: Iterates until no change: an unsatisfied `requires` disables a mod, which may in turn unsatisfy its dependents.

nodes.name: apply_conflicts
nodes.summary: Resolves symmetric conflicts — by default the lower-priority (later) mod is skipped, or allow_conflicts downgrades to a warning.

nodes.name: collect_overlaps
nodes.summary: Builds the target-key ownership map across every effect kind and reports keys owned by more than one mod, treating a group of only-composable train_list hooks as non-overlapping.

nodes.name: tests.rs
nodes.summary: Unit tests for dependency resolution: priority/sequence ordering, disabled and requires fixpoint cascades, symmetric conflicts and per-effect overlap semantics.

nodes.name: folders.rs
nodes.summary: Expands folder-form [[asset]] sections into one single-file op per file discovered recursively and sorted, deriving each row's name/dir and refusing duplicate basenames.

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: Mods-dir scanning: finds every `<mods_dir>/<mod>/mod.toml`, parses and validates it, expands asset folders, primes csv row keys and reads the mod's own train CSVs, skipping broken mods loudly.

nodes.name: tests.rs
nodes.summary: Unit tests for mods-dir scanning: ordering, csv row-key priming, asset-folder expansion and duplicate detection, and the skip-bad-manifests-not-fatal behaviour.

nodes.name: train.rs
nodes.summary: The [[train]] compiler: turns a declared train into an allocated spec-row id and FORM name, four derived csvp rows, three preview icons and the visibility/injection effect keys — pure, no game memory.

nodes.name: overrides_and_sequence
nodes.summary: Checks priority overrides and an explicit sequence order the plan as expected.

nodes.name: requires_fixpoint_cascades
nodes.summary: Checks that an unsatisfied requirement cascades through dependents to a fixpoint.

nodes.name: conflicts_symmetric_default_skips_lower_priority
nodes.summary: Checks symmetric conflicts skip the lower-priority mod by default.

nodes.name: overlap_first_owner_wins
nodes.summary: Checks the first owner of an overlapped target keeps it and later effects are refused.

nodes.name: train_list_hooks_compose_without_overlap
nodes.summary: Checks several train_list hook contributions compose without an overlap.

nodes.name: data_effect_overlaps_refuse_later_mods
nodes.summary: Checks data-effect overlaps (pack/csv/asset) refuse the later mods.

nodes.name: loose_asset_overlap_is_per_pattern
nodes.summary: Checks loose-asset overlap keys are per pattern.

nodes.name: csv_row_patch_overlaps_are_per_row
nodes.summary: Checks `mode = "rows"` csv overlaps are keyed per row so different rows coexist.

nodes.name: folder_root
nodes.summary: Derives the three renderings of a folder-form path: mod-relative `/` form, `\`-joined dir fallback and the directory to walk.

nodes.name: expand_asset_folders
nodes.summary: Expands every folder-form [[asset]] section into ordinary single-file ops so nothing downstream sees the folder form.

nodes.name: expand_one_folder
nodes.summary: Walks one folder recursively and sorted, deriving each file's row name/dir and refusing two files with the same basename.

nodes.name: collect_files
nodes.summary: Recursively collects regular files under a directory as `/`-joined paths relative to a base, sorted.

nodes.name: scan

nodes.name: read_train_csv

nodes.name: prime_csv_row_keys
nodes.summary: Fills each `mode = "rows"` csv section's row keys from its patch file so the resolver can key per-row overlaps.

nodes.name: scans_parses_and_sorts
nodes.summary: Checks scanning parses mods and returns them in sorted directory order.

nodes.name: primes_row_keys_for_row_mode_csv_sections
nodes.summary: Checks row keys are primed from a row-mode csv patch file.

nodes.name: primes_row_keys_from_a_utf8_patch_file
nodes.summary: Checks row keys are primed from a UTF-8 patch file.

nodes.name: unreadable_patch_file_leaves_keys_empty
nodes.summary: Checks an unreadable patch file leaves row keys empty (fail-safe).

nodes.name: expands_asset_folder_recursive_deterministic_dirs
nodes.summary: Checks asset-folder expansion is recursive, sorted and derives dirs correctly.

nodes.name: asset_folder_from_mod_root_uses_explicit_dir
nodes.summary: Checks a folder that is the mod root falls back to the section's explicit dir.

nodes.name: asset_folder_duplicate_basenames_are_a_hard_error
nodes.summary: Checks two files with the same basename in one folder are a hard error.

nodes.name: asset_folder_duplicate_across_sections_is_refused
nodes.summary: Checks duplicate asset names across sections are refused.

nodes.name: missing_asset_folder_is_refused
nodes.summary: Checks a missing asset folder is refused.

nodes.name: bad_manifests_are_skipped_loudly_not_fatal
nodes.summary: Checks a broken manifest is skipped loudly while other mods still load.

nodes.name: TrainRows
nodes.summary: The four derived csvp rows of one train: one row each for form/comment/custom and a whole 10-row group plus separator for pattern.

nodes.name: IconAsset
nodes.summary: One preview-icon asset: the derived i.dat row name and the mod-relative payload file.

nodes.name: CompiledTrain
nodes.summary: One compiled [[train]]: allocated id/FORM name, donor, display names, model, scalars, the derived rows and the icon assets.

nodes.name: effect_keys
nodes.summary: The effect keys a compiled train registers for overlap/priority: the composable train_list hook, the spec-row injection and the three icon assets (deliberately no csv keys).

nodes.name: form_payload
nodes.summary: Serializes the train_form row as a `mode = "rows"` CSV payload.

nodes.name: comment_payload
nodes.summary: Serializes the train_comment row as a `mode = "rows"` CSV payload.

nodes.name: custom_payload
nodes.summary: Serializes the train_custom row as a `mode = "rows"` CSV payload.

nodes.name: pattern_payload
nodes.summary: Serializes the positional train_pattern group-append payload.

nodes.name: fold_upper
nodes.summary: Folds a mod id or key into the FORM-name alphabet: upper-case ASCII alphanumerics, everything else to `_`.

nodes.name: form_name
nodes.summary: Allocates a train's FORM name as FORM_<MODID>_<KEY>, upper-cased.

nodes.name: compile
nodes.summary: Compiles every [[train]] of one mod from a base id upward, skipping malformed trains loudly so the others still load.

nodes.name: compile_one
nodes.summary: Compiles one [[train]]: validates key/name/donor/model/cars/speeds, allocates the id and FORM name, derives the icon trio and the four rows.

nodes.name: effect_keys_of
nodes.summary: Returns the effect keys of every valid train of a mod, for the resolver's overlap registration.

nodes.name: overlay_csv_rows
nodes.summary: Overlays a mod's own vanilla-format CSV rows on a compiled train's derived rows, keyed by FORM name, and refreshes the scalars the car build uses.

nodes.name: compile_all
nodes.summary: Compiles every enabled mod's trains in resolved order, threading the id base across mods and collecting one refusal line per skipped train.

nodes.name: derive_rows
nodes.summary: Builds the four derived rows with the shipped layouts: 29-column train_form (with the 有効/特殊車両フラグ invalidation traps), the 10-row-plus-separator train_pattern group, 11-column train_comment and 19-column train_custom.

nodes.name: clamp.rs
nodes.summary: The always-on save-id clamp guard: bounds both the saved formation group-head id and every per-car id to the live spec-table row count, so a save referencing an id past the vector's end degrades to the engine's own invalid-row state instead of reading past the heap block. Deliberately not behind a config flag — it is a behaviour fix, not a diagnostic.
nodes.languageNotes: Splices the game's own choke points with same-image relay caves plus hand-written global_asm! shims, rather than trampolines, because the head site has no room and the ABI alignment must be reproduced exactly.

nodes.name: formreadout.rs
nodes.summary: Fixes the custom train-form editor's candidate list: rewrites the second vanilla-whitelist scan so the 全て/オリジナル/インポート sub-views ask the loader's composed keep-bitmap instead of the 97-entry vanilla purchase whitelist. Without it, every mod train the composed filter admitted is missing from that editor.

nodes.name: forms.rs
nodes.summary: Pure, host-testable parsing of the exe's FORM name list and of per-mod allow-list files, plus the keep-bitmap build and the multi-mod `compose_filter` that merges several `train_list` contributions into ONE filter bitmap.
nodes.languageNotes: Deliberately free of Windows APIs so the parsing and bitmap logic is unit-testable on any host; the in-file tests are the only tests in this batch.

nodes.name: forward.rs
nodes.summary: Forwards the 10 VERSION.dll exports the proxy must provide to the real system DLL, loading it lazily on the first forwarded call so nothing runs inside DllMain under the loader lock.
nodes.languageNotes: A `forwarder!` macro generates each export; a missing real function returns 0 rather than failing the call.

nodes.name: handlers.rs
nodes.summary: Effect handlers: the in-game `train_list` filter (the only loader code that runs inside the game's own call path) plus the boot-time executors for `[[patch]]` and `[[hook]]` — every write expect-verified, every raw-RVA target readability-guarded, every failure a logged Err instead of a panic.

nodes.name: injector.rs
nodes.summary: The `pack_serving = "inject"` mode: window-scoped injection into the family-B loader's worker-row pool, appending a mod's decoded image blocks straight into the pool the game's loader threads consume — no re-encode, no cache file, nothing on disk.
nodes.languageNotes: Relies on the loader being sequential single-threaded: pack identity is a last-open capture, and the injected region is written once before the runner call and only read afterwards.

nodes.name: lib.rs
nodes.summary: Crate root and product entry point: declares the loader modules (most of them Windows-only) and DllMain, which boots the engine on DLL_PROCESS_ATTACH and always returns 1 so the game can never be blocked from starting.

nodes.name: log.rs
nodes.summary: The loader log (`<mods_dir>/a9loader.log`): one timestamped, severity-tagged line per event, size-capped with a once-per-run rotation check, creating the mods dir lazily and never panicking or failing the boot.

nodes.name: row_count
nodes.summary: Reads the live spec-vector row count from the manager singleton (`([end]-[begin])/0x140`), returning None when the manager is unreadable or the count is implausible — so the clamp stays correct after injection grows the vector.

nodes.name: note_slot
nodes.summary: Logs the once-per-boot debug line for a repaired zero car slot, naming the live crash it prevents (the car wiring computes slot-1 and would walk a wild index).

nodes.name: note_clamp
nodes.summary: Records one clamp per site and emits what it warrants: the per-site info line (once), one debug line per distinct original id, and flood-proof 10/100/1000 count milestones.

nodes.name: head_clamp
nodes.summary: The group-head clamp: returns the id unchanged when in range (or when the manager is unreadable) and otherwise substitutes row 417, the engine's own auto-named invalid row whose blank branch degrades safely.

nodes.name: clamp_car_block
nodes.summary: Clamps the ten per-car u16 ids in the freshly read 0xf8 block and repairs a zero slot to its 1-based position; inert for in-range ids and for unused (id 0) entries.

nodes.name: car_stub
nodes.summary: The spliced car reader: forwards the caller's exact arguments to the original `mmf_paged_read`, clamps the returned block only when it is the fixed 0xf8 car section, and returns the original's own result.

nodes.name: install
nodes.summary: Installs both clamps: expect-verifies the head region and the car call site, writes the head relay cave plus the rewritten `call;nop;nop` region, and splices the car `E8` — publishing runtime state before any splice so a partial failure leaves the stubs unreachable.

nodes.name: install
nodes.summary: Installs the custom-train-form editor fix: expect-verifies the 25-byte vanilla-whitelist scan and the relay cave, then rewrites the scan to call the composed keep-test, so the editor's base-form sub-views stop consulting the vanilla 97 table.

nodes.name: parse_form_list
nodes.summary: Parses the exe's raw UTF-16, comma-separated FORM list (stopping at the first NUL) into names, where the entry's index is its form id.

nodes.name: push_entry
nodes.summary: Trims spaces and tabs from one FORM-list entry and appends it, skipping empty entries — the same trimming the C reference applies.

nodes.name: build_bitmap
nodes.summary: Builds the keep-bitmap from an allow-list: each name is looked up in the FORM list exactly and case-sensitively, with unmatched names counted but otherwise ignored, exactly like the C.

nodes.name: kept
nodes.summary: The keep-bit test for a form id in a filter bitmap; out-of-range ids are always not kept, matching the in-game filter's own rule.

nodes.name: all_forms
nodes.summary: A bitmap keeping every id in `0..forms_len` (capped at FORMS_MAX) — the base layer for deny-only composition.

nodes.name: compose_filter
nodes.summary: Composes every mod's `train_list` contribution into ONE keep-bitmap: the base is the union of allow lists, else the shipped whitelist when any Add exists, else all forms; Deny lists are subtracted last so a deny always wins over an allow or add.
nodes.languageNotes: Order-independent on purpose: a priority tie between two mods must not change which trains are offered.

nodes.name: real_module
nodes.summary: Resolves the real system version.dll by full path (GetSystemDirectoryW + `\version.dll`) and caches it once, lazily on the first forwarded call — never inside DllMain.

nodes.name: real
nodes.summary: Looks one export up in the real system DLL by name, returning None when either the module or the export is missing so the forwarder can return 0 like the C reference.

nodes.name: my_filter
nodes.summary: The in-game filter replacement: keeps only ids with a bitmap bit, writes the new end through `*out` and returns `out` — raw pointers only, no panics, no allocation — plus one per-call trace line naming the dropped ids, which is the observable of trains vanishing after cycling the type filter.

nodes.name: resolve_target
nodes.summary: Resolves a manifest target reference to an RVA plus the expect bytes to verify: from the address book for an anchor, or parsed from the manifest's own hex for a raw RVA.

nodes.name: read_u16s_bounded
nodes.summary: Reads UTF-16 units at an RVA up to (excluding) the first NUL, bounded by a unit limit — the C's bounded scan semantics, also used by the engine's banner cross-check.

nodes.name: verify
nodes.summary: Compares recorded original bytes against live memory at an RVA and refuses with a hex diff when they differ; nothing recorded means nothing to verify, so the check degrades to a no-op.

nodes.name: apply_patch
nodes.summary: Executes one `[[patch]]` effect: resolves the target, verifies the anchor bytes and any extra expect at the offset, then writes the hex data under VirtualProtect — returning the journal line.

nodes.name: apply_hook
nodes.summary: Executes a per-hook effect: only the `nop` handler is served here (train_list contributions are composed once by the engine), verified and then overwritten with the identity remove_if stub.

nodes.name: train_list_contribution
nodes.summary: Parses one mod's `train_list` hook into a contribution: reads the mod-relative list file, builds the id bitmap from the live FORM list and resolves the seam — refusing on a missing or empty list and on an unreadable FORM anchor.

nodes.name: reserved_id_contribution
nodes.summary: Builds a `train_list` contribution that admits explicitly reserved ids — the ids the `[[train]]` compiler allocates — because a name match against the FORM list can never admit an injected row.

nodes.name: read_vanilla_whitelist
nodes.summary: Reads the shipped 97-entry purchase whitelist into a keep-bitmap — the baseline an Add contribution builds on — expect-verified and readability-guarded, so a failure refuses the Add loudly rather than silently offering every form.

nodes.name: install_train_list
nodes.summary: Composes all `train_list` contributions into one keep-bitmap and installs the single filter hook, refusing when contributions disagree on the target RVA and logging a per-contribution breakdown of matched and unmatched names.

nodes.name: plan_ops
nodes.summary: Flattens the engine's inject plan into the stub's op table, lower-casing the pack keys to match the captured `data\<pack>.bin` opens.

nodes.name: install
nodes.summary: Installs the famb splice: verifies the site bytes and pins the original call target to the pool runner, verifies the exe's relay cave, splices the site to the stub and publishes the runtime state — all under the loader lock, before the game's first pack load.

nodes.name: note_pack_open
nodes.summary: The capture seam's receiver: records a `data\<pack>.bin` open when the injector is live and that pack carries ops; a no-op in merge mode, where the runtime state is never installed.

nodes.name: famb_stub
nodes.summary: The spliced family-B call site: for a known, non-failing pack it extends the window with the mod's entries and logs the count; otherwise it crosses the vanilla rows verbatim by calling the runner raw.

nodes.name: row_pool_ok
nodes.summary: Sanity-checks the worker-row pool object (non-null, readable, live refill count) and refuses with a reason so the stub falls back to vanilla untouched.

nodes.name: mark_failing
nodes.summary: Latches a pack as failing, so a pack that failed once logs once and is served vanilla for the rest of the boot.

nodes.name: extend_window
nodes.summary: Validates the vanilla geometry before building anything — row count within the worker capacity, readable last row, non-null delegate, readable shared workspace and a sane vanilla entry count — leaving the pool untouched on any failure.

nodes.name: build_and_attach
nodes.summary: Runs the extension in order: read every payload first, allocate the one shared region, write the vanilla pointer replicate plus our entry blocks, then attach the appended range to the last vanilla row.

nodes.name: read_payloads
nodes.summary: Reads every op's payload from its mod directory; any unreadable file fails the whole pack with the mod and entry named.

nodes.name: alloc_region
nodes.summary: Sizes and VirtualAllocs the one RW region (pointer array plus entry blocks), refusing rather than OOMing the game when the blocks exceed the 256 MiB sanity ceiling.

nodes.name: write_region
nodes.summary: Copies the loader's own vanilla pointer array verbatim and lays out our entry blocks and their array slots after the vanilla range, returning the appended entry count.

nodes.name: attach_row
nodes.summary: Extends the LAST vanilla row — keeping its start, delegate and mode, growing its count and re-pointing its slice at our array (the delegate indexes absolutely, so our blocks land in its extended range) — then records the region for the pack.

nodes.name: write_entry_block
nodes.summary: Writes one entry block in the pack's own layout: a 0x200 UTF-16 name field (NUL-terminated, zero padded), width, height, stored size and the raw decoded payload.

nodes.name: DllMain
nodes.summary: The DLL entry point: boots the loader engine on DLL_PROCESS_ATTACH and always returns 1, so no loader failure can ever keep the game from starting.

nodes.name: Logger
nodes.summary: The loader's log handle: a target path plus a once-per-run rotation flag, exposing line/debug/warn/err severities over one shared emitter.

nodes.name: new
nodes.summary: Creates a logger for a path, arming the once-per-run size check (the mods dir may not exist yet when boot starts).

nodes.name: emit
nodes.summary: Writes one tagged line: creates the mods dir lazily, removes the file once when it exceeds 1 MB, formats HH:MM:SS from GetLocalTime, and appends — never panicking and never failing the boot.

nodes.name: patch.rs
nodes.summary: In-memory patch recipes and the x86-64 splice machinery: VirtualProtect/write/restore/flush writers, the `jmp [rip+0]` relay cave that lets a same-image `E8` reach a stub many GB away, `E8` rel32 splicing with pinned original targets, and the trampoline installer that relocates a prologue and hands the original back as a callable thunk.
nodes.languageNotes: Both hook forms exist because a cross-module `E8 rel32` cannot reach the DLL under wine: the relay cave hops through an in-image thunk using the `jmp [rip+0]; imm64` form.

nodes.name: probe.rs
nodes.summary: Diagnostic, off by default (`probe_fetch = true`): trampoline-only hooks on the four runtime fetch anchors that log which pack object serves which composed key — a question opaque vtable dispatch makes statically unanswerable. It serves nothing and changes no behaviour.
nodes.languageNotes: Each hook's ABI is machine-verified per anchor (not assumed), including the stack-slot out-pointers that must be forwarded untouched.

nodes.name: probe_save.rs
nodes.summary: Diagnostic, off by default (`probe_save = true`): trampoline-only hooks on the four save-side mmf byte writers that answer whether a formation's car block is written as one bulk 0xf8 write (so per-car tails round-trip verbatim) and which caller RVA is the group-record writer.

nodes.name: probe_window.rs
nodes.summary: Diagnostic, off by default (`probe_window = true`): hooks the purchase-window type-tab rebuild and the big list window to dump the spec manager's three index vectors, bracketing the type-cycle quirk and naming the rows that vanish — the mechanism and the fix in one line.
nodes.languageNotes: Dumps only when a size changes (plus the first call): the window runs per frame, so a per-call dump would be noise.

nodes.name: sys.rs
nodes.summary: Minimal hand-declared Win32 surface — the types, constants and roughly a dozen functions the loader needs — plus the two readability guards the whole loader relies on to turn a typo'd RVA into a loud refusal instead of an access violation.
nodes.languageNotes: Hand-declared `extern "system"` bindings, deliberately small; files and the exe path go through std instead.

nodes.name: tabrebuild.rs
nodes.summary: The purchase-window type-tab cycle fix: rewrites the 25-byte vanilla-97 whitelist scan inside the list rebuild so a type tab asks the loader's composed keep-bitmap instead — without it every mod train admitted by the composed filter vanishes on the first cycle and never comes back.

nodes.name: tailgate.rs
nodes.summary: The family-A tailgate: disk-free serving of new `[[asset]]` assets by splicing the game's one family-A LZSS decode funnel and appending the mod's bytes into the shared decoded workspace right after the decode, so the consumers running in the same boot window see them. No re-encode, no cache file.
nodes.languageNotes: Appends at the pack's own DECLARED size, not the runtime decoded length: the decoder runs to exhaustion and leaves a deterministic few bytes of tail junk that no i.dat row references, so the append simply overwrites it.

nodes.name: workspace.rs
nodes.summary: Swaps the family-A decode workspace's 200 MB OUT buffer for a larger one allocated with the game's own allocator at the alloc seam, raising the cap before any pack decodes — the only place the ceiling can be lifted, since the decoder is bounded by the cap.
nodes.languageNotes: The new buffer must come from the game's `_aligned_malloc` because the game's teardown frees it with `_aligned_free`, which expects that allocator's header.

nodes.name: jmp_bytes
nodes.summary: Builds the 16-byte hook write `jmp qword ptr [rip+0]; imm64` plus two nops — the imm64 form that reaches a stub anywhere in the address space, unlike an E9 rel32.

nodes.name: write_bytes
nodes.summary: VirtualProtect → copy → restore protection → FlushInstructionCache; returns false without writing anything when VirtualProtect fails, and the caller logs it.

nodes.name: install_relay_cave
nodes.summary: Writes the 14-byte same-image relay thunk (`FF 25` + absolute stub address) into a code cave, verifying the address book's recorded bytes first, and accepts a re-run that finds exactly its own thunk already there (the workspace-swap install re-runs the tailgate install).

nodes.name: splice_to_cave
nodes.summary: Splices one `E8` site's rel32 to an already-installed relay cave: verifies the recorded bytes, requires the site to really be an `E8`, optionally pins the computed original call target, and rewrites only the four rel32 bytes so call semantics are preserved exactly.

nodes.name: splice_call
nodes.summary: The one-cave-one-site convenience: install the relay cave and splice the site to it, returning the original call target — the common case for hooking a call that must reach a stub many GB away.

nodes.name: Trampoline
nodes.summary: A callable handle to an original function behind an installed hook: the saved prologue bytes plus a jump back past the hook, held as an integer so it is Send/Sync and lives for the process lifetime.

nodes.name: install_trampoline
nodes.summary: Installs a hook over an anchor and returns a trampoline to the original: refuses anchors whose prologue reads RSP as a value (a relocated prologue would corrupt the frame — a live crash), verifies the recorded bytes, then copies the prologue into executable memory and overwrites the entry.

nodes.name: install
nodes.summary: Installs the fetch probe: expect-verifies and trampolines each recorded anchor in order, publishing the trampoline slots before the first hook write; individual refusals log loudly and are skipped, and only a total failure returns Err.

nodes.name: wide_str_indirect
nodes.summary: Reads a wide string that may be either a bare string pointer or a wstring object whose first field is the data pointer, deciding by head sanity (game keys are ASCII paths) and returning None when neither encoding reads cleanly.

nodes.name: my_pack_fetch
nodes.summary: Logs `pack_fetch` calls (pack object, composed key, destination buffer) and forwards verbatim to the original through the trampoline.

nodes.name: my_texture_fetch
nodes.summary: Logs `texture_fetch` calls (ctx, source path, referenced basename, mode) — trying the indirect encoding for both names and logging the raw pointer when neither reads — then forwards verbatim.

nodes.name: my_ccommon_fetch
nodes.summary: Logs `ccommon_fetch` calls with the manager and the name read behind the object, forwarding all six arguments — the two stack out-pointers must reach the original or a cache hit would write through garbage.

nodes.name: my_cache_get
nodes.summary: Logs global fetch-cache gets (cache object and name) and forwards verbatim to the original.

nodes.name: install
nodes.summary: Installs the save-path probe hooks, expect-verifying each anchor independently: a refusal is reported in the returned lines and the other hooks still install, with Err only when nothing installed at all.

nodes.name: peek
nodes.summary: Hex-dumps the leading bytes of a block for a probe line, returning an unreadable marker rather than faulting when the buffer is not mapped.

nodes.name: note
nodes.summary: Records one save-helper call and emits what it warrants: the once-per-distinct-RVA caller-site map, the two verbatim-block lines, capped per-size detail for the watched shapes, the read-side lines, and a periodic call/size histogram.

nodes.name: begin
nodes.summary: Opens one save-side call's log context (helper name, trampoline slot, return address, size, buffer) for the per-call shim bodies to hand to `note`.

nodes.name: vec_elems
nodes.summary: Reads a u32 vector's elements for the probe, bounded by the vector's own begin/end pointers and refusing on unreadable or nonsensical memory.

nodes.name: wblock_body
nodes.summary: The write-block shim body: records the u32-vector block write (arg1, vector, return address) through the shared note path.

nodes.name: rvec_body
nodes.summary: The read-side shim body: records `mmf_read_u32_vector` calls, labelled READ-SIDE so they are never confused with writes.

nodes.name: install
nodes.summary: Installs the window probe: reads the vanilla whitelist for the comparison line, then expect-verifies and trampolines the tab-rebuild and window anchors, each refusal logged with its dump disabled.

nodes.name: vec_len
nodes.summary: Reads a spec-manager index vector's element count from its begin/end pointer pair, refusing on unreadable memory.

nodes.name: vec_contents
nodes.summary: Reads up to `cap` u32 elements of a manager index vector into a Vec, so dumps can be diffed to name the rows that appeared or vanished.

nodes.name: sizes
nodes.summary: Reads the manager's three index-vector sizes in one shot (unfiltered, the list the UI reads, and the type-group list) — the observable the whole probe keys on.

nodes.name: row_desc
nodes.summary: Describes one spec row for a dump line: the display-name pointer, its first 40 wide characters, and the row's type byte(s).

nodes.name: dump
nodes.summary: Emits one dump: the manager's three vector sizes plus the UI list's per-row descriptions, tagged by call number and direction.

nodes.name: delta
nodes.summary: Names the rows that appeared or vanished in the UI list since the previous dump — the type-cycle quirk's observable.

nodes.name: vanilla_would_keep
nodes.summary: Counts what the vanilla 97-entry whitelist scan would have kept for this tab, so the probe line can put the mechanism (the vanilla count) next to the fix (the composed keep count).

nodes.name: my_tab_rebuild
nodes.summary: The type-tab rebuild wrapper: dumps the manager before and after the original rebuild and emits the mechanism+fix evidence line naming the tab index, the composed keep count and the vanilla count.

nodes.name: my_window
nodes.summary: The big list window wrapper: a compact per-frame bracket logging the three list sizes on entry and exit whenever they changed, so the frame in which the filter was cycled is identifiable.

nodes.name: is_readable
nodes.summary: True when every page of `[ptr, ptr+len)` is committed and readable, walking regions with VirtualQuery — the guard that turns a typo'd RVA into a loud refusal instead of an access violation mid-boot.

nodes.name: wide_str
nodes.summary: Reads a bounded UTF-16 string at a pointer, requiring its pages to be readable and refusing a runaway string (over 512 chars) rather than guessing at it.

nodes.name: install
nodes.summary: Installs the type-tab fix: expect-verifies the scan region and the relay cave, writes the cave to the composed-keep test, and rewrites the 25-byte scan to `mov r13,r8; mov ecx,edi; call cave; mov r8,r13; test al,al; jnz found; jmp skip`.

nodes.name: SitePlan
nodes.summary: One host's tailgate request: the pack key, the `E8` site with its expect bytes, the vanilla declared append base, the payload parts (or the rendered i.dat row blob) and the i.dat entry-count bump.

nodes.name: InstallPlan
nodes.summary: The whole tailgate request: the LZSS decode funnel address (the stub's call target and every site's pinned original target), the shared relay cave, and one site plan per host to serve.

nodes.name: install
nodes.summary: Installs the tailgate: writes the shared relay cave once, splices each site to it with the decode funnel as the pinned original target, and publishes the runtime plan — a refused site is skipped loudly and falls back to merge, while a cave failure is fatal.

nodes.name: tailgate_stub
nodes.summary: The spliced decode wrapper: calls the original decoder with the caller's exact arguments, then — only for a known site, a live plan and a clean decode — appends the host's bytes and returns the decoder's own AL.

nodes.name: append_host
nodes.summary: Post-decode validation before committing: the decoded length must reach the plan's declared base (a shorter decode is refused, a longer one is the decoder's overwritten tail junk), the destination must be the shared workspace, the append range must be live, and the declared-size word readable.

nodes.name: commit_append
nodes.summary: Commits the append: the host's parts at `dest+declared`, then (i.dat only) the entry-count bump, then the journal line; returns the decoder's own AL untouched.

nodes.name: hard_fail
nodes.summary: Loud-once hard failure: names the host and the reason, latches the plan so nothing further is attempted for it, and returns the decoder's AL untouched (fail-open).

nodes.name: workspace_stub
nodes.summary: The spliced alloc-tail wrapper: confirms the shipped caps are still in place (proving the address really is the workspace), allocates the bigger OUT buffer with the game's own `_aligned_malloc`, publishes it plus the raised cap and releases the game's buffer — every failure leaves the workspace untouched.

nodes.name: install
nodes.summary: Arms the workspace swap at boot: resolves the anchors, installs the relay cave and splices the alloc tail with its pinned target, stashes the runtime addresses, and returns the journal line.

nodes.name: target_size
nodes.summary: Decides the OUT buffer size: 0 keeps the game's buffer, auto grows only when the planned family-A content does not fit the shipped cap (plus slack for the game's own use), a positive config value forces that size, and the result is clamped to what the u32 cap field can express.

nodes.name: asset.rs
nodes.summary: Implements `extract-asset` and `merge-assets`, the shipped-asset authoring pair: it recovers a shipped i.dat row's host pack (explicit, embedded dir index, or a per-kind content scan) and dumps its raw payload, and it builds the exact merged host pack plus merged i.dat a mod's `[[asset]]` sections would produce.

nodes.name: classify.rs
nodes.summary: Classifies each mod data effect by the boot stage that consumes it (`early:<window>`, `pre-shader/pre-csv`, `unknown`) to answer whether a texture replace actually reaches the game; it encodes the verified two-stage boot pack order and the in-window consumers of each pack.

nodes.name: csv.rs
nodes.summary: `extract-csv` and `patch-csv`: pulls one table out of the game's data/csvp.bin (verbatim UTF-16 or a UTF-8 view) and applies `mode = "rows"` row patches offline, the authoring dry-run of the loader's boot-time merge.

nodes.name: diff.rs
nodes.summary: `diff-pack` and `diff-csv`: compares a vanilla base against a repacked result and emits a ready-to-ship mod dir (mod.toml + payload files), optionally shipping only the changed rows as a `mode = "rows"` patch; removed entries or tables are refused loudly.

nodes.name: Extracted
nodes.summary: An extracted shipped asset: its i.dat name, consumer dir, resolved host pack, byte range, payload bytes, and how the host was resolved.

nodes.name: data_dir
nodes.summary: Resolves the game's `data` directory from either a game dir or the data dir itself, erroring when no pack dir is found.

nodes.name: find_exe
nodes.summary: Locates an `ATrain9*.exe` in a directory to recover the build id needed for auto host resolution.

nodes.name: payload_kind_ok
nodes.summary: Strong per-kind payload check (image magic, `ADX0` chunk length, a whole-blob UTF-16 name list, a text shape) used by the host content scan to reject false `(off, len)` hits.

nodes.name: utf16_name_list_ok
nodes.summary: Validates that a blob is a whole-blob UTF-16 name list — the `.dir` payload shape.

nodes.name: scan_host
nodes.summary: Content-scans a family-A pack's decoded buffer for a plausible payload at `(off, len)`, returning the matched kind.

nodes.name: resolve_host
nodes.summary: Resolves a row's host pack, most authoritative first: the explicit `--pack`, the embedded per-build dir index, then a content scan over every family-A pack.

nodes.name: extract
nodes.summary: Dumps one shipped i.dat row's raw payload by resolving its host pack and writing the exact `(off, len)` bytes.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Entry point for `extract-asset`: resolves the game dir, extracts the named row, and writes it verbatim.

nodes.name: MergedRow
nodes.summary: One synthesized i.dat row of a merged asset: name, consumer dir, host pack, byte range, and whether it overrides a vanilla row.

nodes.name: resolve_ops
nodes.summary: Turns a manifest's `[[asset]]` sections into ordered merge ops, expanding asset folders and resolving `host = "auto"` through the embedded dir index.

nodes.name: merge
nodes.summary: Builds the merged host pack(s) and merged i.dat for one mod's `[[asset]]` sections.

nodes.name: merge_host
nodes.summary: Appends a host pack's mod payloads to its decoded stream and rewrites the affected i.dat rows.

nodes.name: write_merged_idat
nodes.summary: Serializes and writes the merged i.dat index from the synthesized rows.

nodes.name: run_merge
nodes.summary: Entry point for `merge-assets`: creates the output dir and writes the merged packs and i.dat.

nodes.name: Pat
nodes.summary: A name-pattern matcher with equality, prefix, suffix and substring variants, used by the classification rules.

nodes.name: Early
nodes.summary: A boot window in the pack load sequence (Tp/Sdp/Famb/Models/Vp) with its ordinal position.

nodes.name: Class
nodes.summary: The classification verdict kind: early-in-a-window, pre-shader/pre-csv, or unknown.

nodes.name: Row
nodes.summary: One classified data effect: mod id, mechanism, target, class, and the human-readable reason.

nodes.name: Summary
nodes.summary: Aggregated classification counts (early/pre/unknown plus per-window tallies) with a compact one-line rendering.

nodes.name: Verdict
nodes.summary: A per-manifest classification verdict: the overall class and its reason.

nodes.name: window
nodes.summary: Returns the boot window a pack belongs to, if any.

nodes.name: label
nodes.summary: Renders a `Class` as a short human-readable label.

nodes.name: line
nodes.summary: Renders one classification `Row` as a report line.

nodes.name: of
nodes.summary: Aggregates a slice of classification rows into a `Summary` of class counts and window tallies.

nodes.name: compact
nodes.summary: Renders a `Summary` as a compact single line.

nodes.name: all_known
nodes.summary: Reports whether a summary contains no unknown-class rows.

nodes.name: classify_entry
nodes.summary: Classifies one entry name within a pack context by applying the ordered rule set (famb texture, preview, tp names, shaders, models, csv).

nodes.name: classify_manifest
nodes.summary: Classifies every data effect of a manifest into rows.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Entry point for `classify`: classifies a single entry, one mod, or a mods dir and prints the resulting table.

nodes.name: rule_shaders
nodes.summary: Classifies shader bytecode entries (csdp/sdp) as consumed inside their shader-compile window.

nodes.name: rule_models
nodes.summary: Classifies model and prop-dir entries by extension and pack as built in-window (mcp/ep/cp).

nodes.name: pack_rows
nodes.summary: Turns a manifest's `[[pack]]` sections into classified rows.

nodes.name: csv_rows
nodes.summary: Turns a manifest's `[[csv]]` sections into classified rows, always pre-csv.

nodes.name: asset_row
nodes.summary: Classifies one `[[asset]]`, including the residency semantics of `host = "auto"`.

nodes.name: print_mod
nodes.summary: Prints one mod's classification table and its overall verdict.

nodes.name: load_mods
nodes.summary: Loads a single manifest or scans a mods dir into mod/manifest pairs.

nodes.name: table_to_utf8
nodes.summary: Renders a UTF-16 csvp table as canonical UTF-8 text with quoted fields and CRLF rows.

nodes.name: extract
nodes.summary: Entry point for `extract-csv`: lists the container's tables or dumps one table verbatim or as a UTF-8 view.

nodes.name: patch
nodes.summary: Entry point for `patch-csv`: applies `mode = "rows"` patch files to a shipped table offline and reports the merge.

nodes.name: write_entry_payload
nodes.summary: Writes one pack entry's payload to a filesystem-safe file under the output mod dir.

nodes.name: write_mod
nodes.summary: Assembles and writes a generated mod's mod.toml plus its payload files.

nodes.name: diff_pack
nodes.summary: Compares two family-B image packs and emits a `[[pack]]` mod for every added or changed entry, refusing removals.

nodes.name: diff_csv
nodes.summary: Compares two csvp containers and emits a `[[csv]]` mod, optionally as row-level patches under `--rows`.

nodes.name: diff_one_table
nodes.summary: Diffs one CSV table and emits either a whole-table payload or a `mode = "rows"` row patch.

nodes.name: diff_rows
nodes.summary: Computes the replaced and added rows between a base and a modded table.

nodes.name: list_keys
nodes.summary: Formats the replaced and added row keys for a report line.

nodes.name: gen_builds.rs
nodes.summary: `gen-builds`: regenerates the build address book's core anchor set from a live exe with provenance (source exe, file hash, date), and `--check` verifies an existing book matches the exe exactly as an update-day drift check.

nodes.name: gen_dirindex.rs
nodes.summary: `gen-dirindex`: recovers the per-build `dir -> pack` mapping empirically by decoding every shipped pack and testing each i.dat row's `(off, len)` payload against per-kind signature checks, then aggregating per dir and reporting ambiguous or unverified dirs.

nodes.name: inspect.rs
nodes.summary: `inspect`: decodes one pack file and describes it — family, file/decoded sizes, the family-A declared output size, and its container entries (the first 40 unless `--all`).

nodes.name: list.rs
nodes.summary: `list` and `doctor`, the two offline game-dir views: both build the resolution report; `doctor` additionally checks version.dll presence and prints the tail of the last boot's loader log.

nodes.name: core_anchors
nodes.summary: Returns the core anchor set (name, RVA, note, fingerprint length) for a build id.

nodes.name: rva_to_file
nodes.summary: Converts an RVA to a file offset through the PE section table, per section rather than by a blanket delta.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Entry point for `gen-builds`: resolves the exe identity, then checks or emits the address book.

nodes.name: emit_book
nodes.summary: Renders the address book text with provenance (exe, hash, date) for the given anchors.

nodes.name: check_book
nodes.summary: Verifies that an existing address book matches the exe exactly — the update-day drift check.

nodes.name: Kind
nodes.summary: A row's content kind (`.x`/`.att`/`.dir`/texture/csv/other) with a `strong` signal flag and display formatting.

nodes.name: Report
nodes.summary: The generator's findings: packs, decode failures, rows, matched rows, kind tallies, dir resolutions and train-dir statistics.

nodes.name: of
nodes.summary: Classifies a row name into a content `Kind`.

nodes.name: fmt
nodes.summary: Renders a `Kind` for display.

nodes.name: row_matches
nodes.summary: Tests whether a decoded pack buffer plausibly holds a row's payload at `(off, len)`, using per-kind signature checks.

nodes.name: utf16_name_run
nodes.summary: Measures a UTF-16 name run in a buffer, the `.dir` shape signal.

nodes.name: resolve_dir
nodes.summary: Resolves a dir to its unique host pack, or marks it ambiguous when its rows span packs.

nodes.name: find_exe
nodes.summary: Locates the game exe next to a data dir to obtain the build id.

nodes.name: generate
nodes.summary: Drives index generation: build identity, read rows, decode packs, match rows, aggregate.

nodes.name: read_rows
nodes.summary: Reads and parses the shipped i.dat rows from a data dir.

nodes.name: pack_keys
nodes.summary: Enumerates the decodable pack keys present in a data dir.

nodes.name: match_rows
nodes.summary: Matches every shipped row against every decoded pack buffer, tracking which pack holds each row.

nodes.name: aggregate
nodes.summary: Aggregates per-row hits into per-dir resolutions, ambiguous dirs and train-dir statistics.

nodes.name: summarize
nodes.summary: Builds the generation report summary from rows, hits and the aggregation.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Entry point for `gen-dirindex`: generates or checks the dir index table.

nodes.name: emit_table
nodes.summary: Renders the `dir -> pack` index table with provenance.

nodes.name: report_text
nodes.summary: Renders the human-readable generation report.

nodes.name: write_or_check
nodes.summary: Writes the generated table, or verifies that an existing one matches — the update-day check.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Entry point for `inspect`: decodes one pack and prints its family, sizes, declared output size and container entries.

nodes.name: list
nodes.summary: Entry point for `list`: prints the offline resolution report in verbose form.

nodes.name: doctor
nodes.summary: Entry point for `doctor`: prints the resolution report, checks version.dll presence, and tails the last boot's loader log.

nodes.name: mkpack.rs
nodes.summary: `mkpack`: builds a pack file from raw payloads in four container kinds (family-B images/csvs, a family-A opaque stream, and a family-A i.dat index) and byte-verifies the result by decoding and re-parsing it before writing.

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: Module barrel declaring the subcommand implementation modules; main.rs owns the clap argument model and dispatches into these, so no implementation lives at the crate root.

nodes.name: report.rs
nodes.summary: The offline resolution report shared by `list` and `doctor`: it performs the dry run (read config, scan mods, resolve the load order and auto hosts) and renders it through one small function per printed section, including auto-host resolution and asset collision checks.

nodes.name: selftests.rs
nodes.summary: Synthetic self-tests for the format library, run by `verify` before the real-pack sweep: cipher + md5 header, LZSS (overlap and ring wrap), image/csv container byte parity, i.dat parity, the full family-B pack pipeline, and savegame member carving.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Entry point for `mkpack`: builds the chosen container kind and byte-verifies it before writing.

nodes.name: build_images
nodes.summary: Builds a family-B image container from `NAME=W:H:FILE` specs.

nodes.name: build_csvs
nodes.summary: Builds a family-B csv container from `NAME=FILE` specs.

nodes.name: build_idat
nodes.summary: Builds a family-A i.dat index container from `NAME:DIR:LEN:OFF` specs.

nodes.name: Offline
nodes.summary: Everything the offline report needs, gathered once: config, exe/build identity, scanned mods, manifests, dirs, errors and auto-host resolutions.

nodes.name: find_game_exe
nodes.summary: Finds the game executable in a game dir to recover the build id.

nodes.name: offline_resolution
nodes.summary: Performs the offline dry run: reads the config, resolves the exe build, scans mods, and resolves the load order and auto hosts.

nodes.name: print_common
nodes.summary: Renders the shared header sections of the list/doctor report.

nodes.name: print_identity
nodes.summary: Prints the game and build identity section of the report.

nodes.name: print_config
nodes.summary: Prints the loader config section of the report.

nodes.name: print_pack_serving
nodes.summary: Prints the pack-serving section, explaining where each pack's effects reach the game.

nodes.name: print_resolution
nodes.summary: Prints the mod resolution order and the per-mod gate verdicts.

nodes.name: print_mod
nodes.summary: Prints one mod's detail section: the order line, the classify roll-up and the csv/asset roll-ups.

nodes.name: print_csv_rollup
nodes.summary: Prints the CSV effect roll-up for one mod.

nodes.name: print_host_auto
nodes.summary: Prints the auto-host resolutions for one mod, flagging refusals and unknown builds.

nodes.name: print_asset_collisions
nodes.summary: Prints asset collisions between a mod's assets and vanilla or other mods.

nodes.name: print_asset_payload_check
nodes.summary: Prints the offline payload existence check for a mod's assets.

nodes.name: print_loose_rollup
nodes.summary: Prints the loose-asset roll-up for one mod.

nodes.name: print_mod_verbose
nodes.summary: Prints the verbose per-mod section, including the classification rows.

nodes.name: self_tests
nodes.summary: The ordered list of synthetic format-library self-tests; the order is the report's order.

nodes.name: test_containers
nodes.summary: Proves image and csv container byte parity, including verbatim name fields and the garbage padding some original packs carry.

nodes.name: test_idat
nodes.summary: Proves i.dat serialize/parse parity for both known build paddings.

nodes.name: test_pack_pipeline
nodes.summary: Proves the full family-B pack pipeline end to end (encode/decode round-trip).

nodes.name: trains.rs
nodes.summary: `trains`: the offline `[[train]]` dry run — compiles every declared train (across the resolved load order or a single mod) and prints its allocated id and FORM name, the four derived rows, the icons, the effect keys and the offline validation checks.

nodes.name: verify.rs
nodes.summary: `verify`: proves the format library against real packs — runs the synthetic self-tests, then sweeps each data dir with decrypt/decode/container-invariant/round-trip/rebuild-parity checks, optionally byte-differential against the C oracle (a9enc / a9dec).

nodes.name: main.rs
nodes.summary: The a9ml CLI surface: the clap argument model ([`Cli`] / [`Cmd`]) holding every subcommand's names, flags, defaults and help text as the user-visible contract, plus the dispatch to one entry point per subcommand.

nodes.name: util.rs
nodes.summary: Small stateless helpers shared across the generators: a dependency-free UTC `civil_stamp` and an `ascii_like` byte heuristic, each deduplicated from the modules that used to carry their own copy.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Entry point for `trains`: compiles every declared train (across the load order or one mod) and prints the allocation, derived rows, icons, effect keys and validation checks.

nodes.name: print_train
nodes.summary: Prints one compiled train's allocation, derived rows, icons and effect keys.

nodes.name: read_shipped_forms
nodes.summary: Reads the shipped FORM name catalog from the game exe so a mod train's name can be checked for collisions.

nodes.name: parse_forms
nodes.summary: Parses the shipped UTF-16 comma-separated FORM name list into units.

nodes.name: Check
nodes.summary: One named pass/fail line in the verify report, with an optional note.

nodes.name: ok
nodes.summary: Constructs a passing `Check`.

nodes.name: fail
nodes.summary: Constructs a failing `Check`.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Entry point for `verify`: self-tests, oracle resolution, one sweep per data dir, the expect-rebuild completeness check and the verdict.

nodes.name: parse_expectations
nodes.summary: Parses the `--expect-rebuild` keys into expectation records.

nodes.name: resolve_oracle
nodes.summary: Resolves the C oracle binary directory (a9enc/a9dec) used for the byte-differential checks.

nodes.name: sweep_dir
nodes.summary: Sweeps one data dir: decodes and checks every recognized pack, reporting unrecognized basenames as skipped.

nodes.name: check_pack
nodes.summary: Runs the per-pack checks: decrypt, decode, container invariants, our-encoder round-trip, rebuild parity and the oracle differential.

nodes.name: check_container
nodes.summary: Verifies a decoded pack's container invariants.

nodes.name: oracle_encode
nodes.summary: Runs the C oracle encoder on a temp payload for byte-differential comparison.

nodes.name: oracle_decode
nodes.summary: Runs the C oracle decoder for byte-differential comparison.

nodes.name: Cmd
nodes.summary: The clap subcommand enum defining every a9ml subcommand with its flags, defaults and help text — the user-visible contract.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Parses the CLI and dispatches to one entry point per subcommand, printing any error and exiting non-zero.

nodes.name: civil_stamp
nodes.summary: A `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` UTC stamp via a hand-rolled proleptic-Gregorian conversion, keeping the tool free of a chrono dependency.

nodes.name: ascii_like
nodes.summary: Heuristically reports whether a byte buffer looks like ASCII/control text.

nodes.name: add.rs
nodes.summary: Byte-for-byte transcription of the pack cipher's 256-byte ADD translation table, recovered from the international Steam exe at file offset 0x697310 and cross-checked against a live memory probe and values recovered from shipped packs.
nodes.languageNotes: The entire file is one `#[rustfmt::skip] pub const [u8; 256]`, kept as literal rows so the table can be diffed against the exe by eye.

nodes.name: container.rs
nodes.summary: Family-B container codecs: the verbatim-preserving 0x200 UTF-16 name field plus parse/serialize for both entry-table shapes — image packs (`[w][h][stored][payload]`) and the 0x204 CSV variant (`[len][data]`) used by csvp/sdp/csdp.
nodes.languageNotes: Name fields are stored as raw bytes and only decoded for display, because ARTDINK's own serializer leaves filename fragments in the padding after the NUL — decode-then-re-encode would not be lossless.

nodes.name: crypt.rs
nodes.summary: The pack cipher: an MD5(plaintext) 16-byte header that doubles as the XOR key, the ADD-table keystream, and both cipher directions plus the header check that rejects foreign packs.

nodes.name: csv.rs
nodes.summary: UTF-16 CSV table codec and the row-merge tier: verbatim-preserving parse/serialize of a csvp table blob plus keyed row patching, positional group append and whole-table replace.
nodes.languageNotes: Rows keep their original bytes and line terminator alongside the decoded fields, so only rows a patch actually touches are re-encoded — the reason a no-op merge is byte-identical.

nodes.name: idat.rs
nodes.summary: The `i.dat` master asset index: parse/serialize of the `adzpidx00` header, the per-entry name/dir records and the 9-byte tail, plus the row writer that appends new family-A assets and bumps the entry count.

nodes.name: lib.rs
nodes.summary: Crate root of a9-formats: declares the format codec modules (cipher, LZSS, pack framing, containers, CSV, i.dat, savegame, overlay) and the shared `Error` type every codec returns.

nodes.name: lzss.rs
nodes.summary: The LZSS codec: a decode that is byte-exact against the game's loader at 0x140314bf0 with read-as-you-write back-references, and a greedy 22-bit hash-chain encoder that is byte-identical to the reference packer.

nodes.name: csvs.rs
nodes.summary: The csvp merge shape: whole-table replaces, keyed row patches and positional group appends applied to the 0x204 CSV container, decoded then merged then re-encoded under a decode-budget check.

nodes.name: NameField
nodes.summary: A raw 0x200-byte UTF-16 name field that stores the bytes verbatim, decodes only for display, and re-serializes exactly what it parsed — what makes parse→serialize byte-identical on ARTDINK's garbage-padded packs.

nodes.name: ImageEntry
nodes.summary: Decoded view of one family-B image entry: the name field, the declared width/height and the stored payload.

nodes.name: CsvEntry
nodes.summary: One entry of the 0x204 CSV container variant (csvp/sdp/csdp): a name field plus a single variable-length table blob.

nodes.name: from_str
nodes.summary: Builds a clean, zero-padded name field from a string, refusing a name that overflows the fixed 0x200-byte field.

nodes.name: as_str
nodes.summary: Lossy UTF-16 decode of the name field up to the first NUL — used for display and logging, never for re-serialization.

nodes.name: dds_dims
nodes.summary: Reads width and height straight out of a DDS header (offsets 12 and 16) so a merged image entry carries the true dimensions.

nodes.name: parse_images
nodes.summary: Walks the image-pack entry table (count, then per entry name field, dimensions, stored length and payload), requiring the walk to consume the buffer exactly.

nodes.name: serialize_images
nodes.summary: Re-emits the image entry table: the count, then each entry's stored name-field bytes, dimensions and payload length.

nodes.name: parse_csvs
nodes.summary: Walks the 0x204 CSV container (count, then per entry a name field and a u32-length-prefixed table blob), consuming the decoded buffer exactly.

nodes.name: serialize_csvs
nodes.summary: Re-emits the CSV container exactly as the reference builder does, preserving each entry's original name-field bytes.

nodes.name: md5
nodes.summary: Thin MD5 wrapper producing the 16-byte digest that is both the pack integrity check and the header XOR key.

nodes.name: decrypt_body
nodes.summary: Decrypts the body after the 16-byte header with `(byte + ADD[i & 0xff]) ^ header[i & 0xf]` — the exact inverse of encrypt_file.

nodes.name: encrypt_file
nodes.summary: Encrypts a plaintext body and prefixes MD5(plaintext) as the header, producing a complete on-disk pack file.

nodes.name: Eol
nodes.summary: The four line terminators a shipped CSV table can use (CRLF/LF/CR/none); a changed row is re-encoded with the base table's dominant one.

nodes.name: Row
nodes.summary: One parsed CSV row: the raw bytes plus its own line terminator kept verbatim, a decoded field view, and a canonical re-encoding used only for changed rows.

nodes.name: Table
nodes.summary: A parsed CSV table (BOM flag plus rows) whose parse/serialize round-trip byte-identically, carrying the row operations: patch keys, dominant EOL, retain and serialize.

nodes.name: MergeMode
nodes.summary: Selects row-merge semantics: `Rows` patches by first-column key, `Replace` takes the last patch for the table wholesale.

nodes.name: MergeStats
nodes.summary: Counters reported by a merge: rows replaced, appended, unchanged, and positionally group-appended.

nodes.name: canonical
nodes.summary: Re-encodes a changed or added row canonically: every field double-quoted with `"` doubled, comma-joined and terminated with the chosen EOL.

nodes.name: patch_keys
nodes.summary: The non-empty first-column keys of every row — the identity set a row patch is matched against.

nodes.name: dominant_eol
nodes.summary: Picks the line terminator most of the table's rows use, so re-encoded rows stay stylistically consistent with the shipped table.

nodes.name: serialize
nodes.summary: Concatenates the BOM and the rows' verbatim bytes, reproducing the base table byte-for-byte when nothing changed.

nodes.name: parse
nodes.summary: Parses a UTF-16LE BOM-prefixed CSV blob into rows, honouring quoted fields with embedded commas and newlines (the train_comment column does exactly that) while keeping each row's raw bytes and terminator.

nodes.name: parse_patch
nodes.summary: Parses a mod's patch file, accepting either plain UTF-8 or BOM-prefixed UTF-16 so authors can ship readable text.

nodes.name: append_group
nodes.summary: Appends a group of rows positionally at the end of a table — the keyless continuation rows (train_pattern groups) that a keyed patch cannot address.

nodes.name: merge_rows
nodes.summary: Applies row patches to a base table: keyed rows replace, unknown keys append, and duplicate keys, empty keys and column mismatches are refused loudly while untouched rows keep their exact bytes.

nodes.name: Idat
nodes.summary: A parsed i.dat: the build-specific header padding kept verbatim plus the entry list, with row lookup and row-append operations.

nodes.name: Entry
nodes.summary: One i.dat index entry: name, dir and the 9-byte tail (u32 v1, u8 v2 and the 4 bytes the loader reads unaligned at +5), all kept verbatim.

nodes.name: NewRow
nodes.summary: A row to be appended to i.dat: name, dir, length, flag and computed offset, serialized into the entry shape with a fresh tail.

nodes.name: write_record
nodes.summary: Serializes one entry as `[size][nameLen][name][dirLen][dir][9-byte tail]`; the size field is what makes the loader's walk self-checking.

nodes.name: tail
nodes.summary: Builds the 9-byte entry tail for a new row — the field the serializer otherwise has to preserve verbatim from real files.

nodes.name: to_bytes
nodes.summary: Renders a NewRow as entry bytes by composing its name, dir and tail.

nodes.name: render_rows
nodes.summary: Renders a batch of NewRows to bytes and reports how many were written.

nodes.name: bump_count
nodes.summary: Increments the u32 entry count in the i.dat header once rows have been appended.

nodes.name: add_rows
nodes.summary: Appends new asset rows to a decoded i.dat, computing each row's offset from the family-A append layout so a row's `off` and its bytes cannot drift apart.

nodes.name: read_str
nodes.summary: Reads a length-prefixed UTF-16 string from the decoded buffer and returns it with the position after it.

nodes.name: parse
nodes.summary: Parses the `adzpidx00` master index: the magic, the build-specific header padding, the count, then entries walked by their own size field.

nodes.name: serialize
nodes.summary: Re-emits i.dat, keeping the header padding and every entry's 9-byte tail verbatim so the round-trip stays byte-identical across builds.

nodes.name: Error
nodes.summary: The crate-wide error enum: too-short input, MD5 header mismatch, family-A declared-size mismatch, container and i.dat walk failures, and oversized name fields.

nodes.name: decode
nodes.summary: Decodes `data[skip..]` to exhaustion through the 4096-byte ring (write cursor starting at 0xfee), copying back-references read-as-you-write so an overlapping reference self-extends instead of corrupting the output.

nodes.name: encode
nodes.summary: Greedy hash-chain LZSS matcher (22-bit hash, max 18-byte matches) producing the bit-exact stream the reference packer builds.

nodes.name: CsvOp
nodes.summary: One `[[csv]]` table operation: the table name, its kind (replace / rows / group-append) and the payload bytes.

nodes.name: CsvOpKind
nodes.summary: Whether a csv op replaces the whole table, key-patches it, or appends a positional group of keyless rows (the train_pattern shape).

nodes.name: overlay_csvp
nodes.summary: Decodes a csvp family-B pack, merges the ops into its tables and re-encodes — the entry point shared by the in-game loader and the a9ml host tools.

nodes.name: group_ops_by_table
nodes.summary: Groups the ops by table name and refuses conflicting duplicates before any merge work happens.

nodes.name: table_payload
nodes.summary: Produces the merged payload for one table — whole-table replace, keyed row merge or positional group append — on top of the existing entry or a freshly parsed table.

nodes.name: overlay_csvs_decoded
nodes.summary: The CSV merge on already-decoded container bytes: parse the 0x204 container, rewrite the touched tables, serialize and assert the decode budget.

nodes.name: family_a.rs
nodes.summary: The family-A append: new asset payloads concatenated onto a size-prefixed stream (vp/tp/mcp/ep/cp), with the pure layout helper the i.dat row writer shares so a row's offset and its bytes cannot drift apart.

nodes.name: images.rs
nodes.summary: Family-B image-entry merges: replace an existing entry's payload and dimensions by name, or append a new entry, in the me*/mt* packs — keeping the original name field verbatim.

nodes.name: listings.rs
nodes.summary: The `.dir` group-listing helpers the loader auto-merges: parse a flat NUL-terminated UTF-16 name run, and extend it with new names while keeping the vanilla bytes verbatim.

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: The overlay module barrel: declares the three merge shapes (images, csvs, family_a) and the listing helpers, re-exports their operations, and defines the `MergeReport` every merge returns.

nodes.name: tests.rs
nodes.summary: The overlay contract tests: byte-level round-trips and loud refusals for image, CSV and family-A merges plus the listing helpers, including an opt-in run against a real shipped pack.

nodes.name: pack.rs
nodes.summary: Pack-file framing for both families: classify a filename, decode/encode family A (`[u32 declared size][LZSS]`) and family B (bare LZSS entry table), all wrapped in the MD5-header cipher.

nodes.name: savegame.rs
nodes.summary: Savegame (`.a9d`/`.a9d5`) plaintext members: carve zlib streams out of a save blob and inflate each one with exact consumed-input accounting.

nodes.name: AssetOp
nodes.summary: One `[[asset]]` op: the payload chunk plus the i.dat row identity (bare master-map key and consumer dir) it will carry.

nodes.name: plan_family_a_lens
nodes.summary: Computes `(offset, length)` for each appended payload from lengths alone — the single source of truth for the family-A append layout, shared with the i.dat row writer.

nodes.name: overlay_pack_a
nodes.summary: Decodes a family-A pack, appends the ops' payloads and re-encodes — the family-A counterpart of overlay_pack_b.

nodes.name: overlay_assets_decoded
nodes.summary: Appends asset payloads to an already-decoded family-A stream and reports the merge, refusing duplicates and an over-budget result.

nodes.name: ImageOp
nodes.summary: One `[[pack.entry]]` op: the entry name, its dimensions and the payload to replace or append.

nodes.name: overlay_pack_b
nodes.summary: Decodes a family-B image pack, merges the ops and re-encodes — the image-pack entry point.

nodes.name: overlay_images_decoded
nodes.summary: The image merge on decoded container bytes: a matching name replaces payload and dimensions while keeping the vanilla name field verbatim, an unknown name appends, and duplicates or an over-budget result are refused.

nodes.name: listing_parse
nodes.summary: Parses a `.dir` listing — a flat run of NUL-terminated UTF-16LE names with no count prefix, stride or padding — refusing odd lengths, a missing final NUL, empty segments and invalid UTF-16 loudly.

nodes.name: listing_extend
nodes.summary: Rebuilds a listing as the vanilla bytes verbatim followed by each new name that is not already listed, so the no-op case is byte-identical.

nodes.name: MergeReport
nodes.summary: The uniform result of every overlay merge: entries added and replaced, the synthesized pack's decoded and encoded sizes, and the csvp row replace/append/group-append counters.

nodes.name: merge_report
nodes.summary: Builds a MergeReport for the non-CSV shapes with the row counters zeroed.

nodes.name: images_add_replace_roundtrip
nodes.summary: Builds a family-B image pack, merges an add and a replace, then decodes the result and asserts the merged entries and their order.

nodes.name: images_duplicate_op_refused
nodes.summary: Asserts that two ops on the same image entry name are refused rather than silently resolved.

nodes.name: csvs_add_replace_roundtrip
nodes.summary: Merges a whole-table add and a whole-table replace into a csvp container and asserts the decoded table payloads.

nodes.name: csvs_row_merge_on_top_of_a_container
nodes.summary: Applies row patches to a table inside a real container and asserts both the patched and the appended rows survive the re-encode.

nodes.name: csvs_row_patch_on_missing_table_is_refused
nodes.summary: Asserts a row patch against a table the container does not have is refused, not silently created.

nodes.name: csvs_two_whole_table_replaces_refused
nodes.summary: Asserts two whole-table replaces for the same table name are refused as a conflict.

nodes.name: family_a_layout_and_append_roundtrip
nodes.summary: Appends payloads to a family-A stream and asserts the planned offsets, the decoded layout and the merge report all agree.

nodes.name: family_a_budget_and_duplicates_refused
nodes.summary: Asserts a family-A append is refused when it exceeds the budget or repeats an asset name.

nodes.name: listing_parse_roundtrips_and_bounds_by_the_payload
nodes.summary: Asserts listing_parse recovers exactly the names in a run and rejects a payload that is not a well-formed name run.

nodes.name: listing_extend_appends_new_and_dedups
nodes.summary: Asserts listing_extend appends only names not already listed and reports the resulting entry count.

nodes.name: listing_extend_noop_is_byte_identical
nodes.summary: Asserts extending a listing with names it already contains returns the vanilla bytes unchanged.

nodes.name: listing_extend_refuses_a_non_utf16_payload_loudly
nodes.summary: Asserts a malformed listing payload is refused with a loud error instead of being patched into.

nodes.name: real_pack_when_available
nodes.summary: Opt-in test that runs an image-entry merge against a real shipped pack when the game install is present.

nodes.name: Family
nodes.summary: The two pack framing families: A = size-prefixed body (tp/mcp/vp/ep/cp/i.dat), B = bare LZSS entry table (me*/mt*/csvp/sdp/csdp).

nodes.name: Container
nodes.summary: Which decoded shape a pack carries (Images, Csvs, Idat, Opaque) — drives container validation.

nodes.name: classify
nodes.summary: Maps a pack filename to its framing family and decoded container shape, so callers know how to validate the body.

nodes.name: decode_pack
nodes.summary: Decrypts a pack file, verifies the MD5 header against the plaintext and LZSS-decodes the body into its decoded form, per family.

nodes.name: family_a_declared_size
nodes.summary: Reads the declared output size from a family-A body without decompressing, applying the reference decoder's tolerance.

nodes.name: encode_pack_a
nodes.summary: Re-encodes a family-A body as `[u32 len][LZSS]` and wraps it with the cipher.

nodes.name: encode_pack
nodes.summary: Dispatches to the family-A or family-B encoder for a decoded body.

nodes.name: carve_members
nodes.summary: Scans a save blob for `78 9C` zlib headers, inflates each member and advances by its true input length, skipping non-member stretches byte by byte.

nodes.name: inflate_member
nodes.summary: Inflates exactly one zlib member from the front of a buffer using flate2's low-level Decompress so the consumed-input count is exact (a streaming Read adapter could read past the member boundary).

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: The boot engine that runs inside DllMain: reads config, identifies the running build from the exe, scans and resolves mods, applies expect-verified memory patches and hooks, plans and installs the overlay, tailgate, injector and train-row injection, and logs the final applied/refused count line.
nodes.languageNotes: Every phase degrades to a loud log line plus 'no effects' instead of aborting the boot; file IO and memory writes only, never LoadLibrary, because this runs under the loader lock.

nodes.name: plan.rs
nodes.summary: The boot's data-plan collector: walks the resolved mods in priority order and folds [[pack]], [[csv]], [[asset]], [[loose_asset]] and [[train]] sections into the overlay serving plan (or the injector plan in inject mode), applying per-effect overlap refusal and counting refusals.

nodes.name: report.rs
nodes.summary: The boot's end-of-run report line: the final count of applied and refused memory effects, stating that the game continues.

nodes.name: tailgate_plan.rs
nodes.summary: The boot-time tailgate planner: derives auto-merged .dir group listings from the mods' own [[asset]] rows, decides per host whether family-A payloads can be appended in place at the decode instead of going through merge, grows the decode workspace when the plan needs more, and installs the shared relay cave plus one site per pack.

nodes.name: boot
nodes.summary: The engine's narrative entry point: config, logger and the loader-off escape hatch, then build gate, save-id clamp, mod scan/resolve, [[train]] compilation with shipped-name collision refusal, memory effects, the data plan, listing and tailgate decisions, the inject splice, the overlay hook, train-row injection, the optional probes and the result line.

nodes.name: config_line
nodes.summary: Formats the one-line config: boot summary naming the mods dir, conflicts mode, log level, pack and asset serving modes, and whether a9loader.toml was present.

nodes.name: build_gate
nodes.summary: Identifies the running game build by fingerprinting the exe file (no version.dll calls under the loader lock) and resolves its embedded address-book entry, returning None with a loud reason for every failure so no memory effect is written against an unknown build.

nodes.name: scan_and_resolve
nodes.summary: Scans mods/, drops disabled ids with one line each, and resolves the survivors through the dependency, conflict and overlap resolver, logging warnings, skips and overlap losers; returns None as a pure proxy when no mods remain, after honouring an explicit workspace_out_mb.

nodes.name: apply_memory_effects
nodes.summary: Applies every mod's [[patch]] and [[hook]] in resolved order and composes the per-mod train_list contributions, including the programmatically added reserved train ids, into one filter install plus the type-tab and form-readout fixes.

nodes.name: apply_mod_effects
nodes.summary: Applies one mod's effects: the game_builds gate first, then each [[patch]] as an expect-verified journaled write and each [[hook]] (train_list hooks become a deferred contribution, others install immediately), counting applied and refused.

nodes.name: install_composed_train_list
nodes.summary: Installs the single composed train_list filter and, on success, arms the type-tab rebuild fix and the custom-train-editor form-readout fix; both are fail-open, so the filter keeps working when they refuse.

nodes.name: note_asset_serving
nodes.summary: Logs which mechanism serves [[asset]] rows when pack_serving is inject and the two serving modes differ, so a reader is not surprised that the family-A tailgate handles the assets.

nodes.name: install_inject
nodes.summary: Installs the family-B injector splice: verifies the famb_runner_call site and relay-cave anchors, installs the stub, and on any refusal moves the inject ops back into the merge plan, returning whether the injector is live.

nodes.name: install_overlay
nodes.summary: Installs the CFile::Open overlay hook when any serving plan is non-empty; a missing cfile_open anchor is a loud fail-open that still names every loose asset it cannot serve.

nodes.name: OverlaySummary::of
nodes.summary: The OverlaySummary constructor: folds the plan into the numbers of the hook-install summary line, covering the entry count, distinct csv tables, asset, listing and loose counts, the touched pack list and the asset/loose log fragments.

nodes.name: install_overlay_hooked
nodes.summary: Installs the cfile_open hook with the verified anchor and logs either the summary line, the inject-capture-only variant, or the loud failure report naming every loose asset left unserved.

nodes.name: report_overlay_failure
nodes.summary: Reports a failed overlay hook install: the refusal line, an inject warning when the capture hook is load-bearing, and one line per loose asset that will serve the original file this boot.

nodes.name: install_probe
nodes.summary: The opt-in fetch probe: collects the probe specs from the address book and installs the diagnostic trampolines; without the probe feature a stub logs one loud refusal instead of hooking anything.

nodes.name: install_window_probe
nodes.summary: The opt-in purchase-window probe: hooks the type-tab rebuild and list-window entries trampoline-only to dump the spec-table manager's index vectors whenever a size changes; feature-gated with a loud stub fallback.

nodes.name: install_save_probe
