nodes.summary: The opt-in save-path probe: hooks the four save-side mmf helpers trampoline-only to log the caller RVA, size and first bytes of every save-path write; feature-gated with a loud stub fallback.

nodes.name: refuse_colliding_trains
nodes.summary: Drops any compiled [[train]] whose allocated FORM name equals a shipped catalog name, because such an alias would make the injected row shadow a real train in the annotator's name-keyed lookup.

nodes.name: install_train_injection
nodes.summary: Converts the compiled trains into rowinject TrainRows and installs the spec-row injection after the overlay is up; a refusal leaves the trains with their CSV and asset effects only (fail-open).

nodes.name: PlanBuilder
nodes.summary: The plan collector that folds every data effect of the resolved mod set into the overlay plan or the injector plan plus a refusal count, holding the resolution, build id, serving mode, logger and compiled trains.

nodes.name: new
nodes.summary: Constructs a PlanBuilder with an empty overlay plan (images, csvs, assets, listings, tailgated, declared, loose), an empty injector plan and a zero refusal count.

nodes.name: add_mod
nodes.summary: Collects one mod's data effects in the documented section order: [[pack]], [[csv]], [[asset]], [[loose_asset]], [[train]].

nodes.name: finish
nodes.summary: Consumes the builder and hands back the overlay plan, the injector plan and the total refusal count.

nodes.name: packs
nodes.summary: [[pack]] handling: only family-B image packs (me*/mt*) carry entries, so their ops go to the injector plan in inject mode and to the merge overlay otherwise, with per-entry overlap refusal; family-A stream packs are refused loudly as [[csv]] or asset territory.

nodes.name: csvs
nodes.summary: [[csv]] handling: reads each patch payload and dispatches to whole-table replace or per-row patch, counting a refusal when the payload cannot be read.

nodes.name: csv_replace
nodes.summary: mode = replace: replaces a whole csvp table with the payload after the table-level overlap check.

nodes.name: csv_rows
nodes.summary: mode = rows: parses the row patch and retains only rows no other mod already owns (per-row overlap refusal), failing safe on the whole-table key when the patch file was unreadable at scan time.

nodes.name: assets
nodes.summary: [[asset]] handling: resolves each host (auto via the embedded per-build dir index), requires a family-A host the loader can append to, applies name-level overlap refusal and emits the AssetOpPlans served through merge or tailgate.

nodes.name: resolve_asset_host
nodes.summary: Resolves one [[asset]] host: an authored host is returned as-is while an auto host goes through the embedded per-build dir index, with a logged, counted refusal at every failure point.

nodes.name: loose
nodes.summary: [[loose_asset]] handling: registers one path pattern per op with case-insensitive pattern-level overlap refusal; the payload itself is materialized later, at overlay install time.

nodes.name: trains
nodes.summary: Expands each compiled [[train]] into primitives that already exist and deliberately emits no csvp rows (the CSV pipeline can never attach rows above its fixed 417-entry per-form buffers), only the three preview-icon [[asset]] rows resolved to the tp pack via the dir index.

nodes.name: result_line
nodes.summary: Formats the boot's final count line: how many memory effects were applied and how many refused, with the game continuing either way.

nodes.name: thousands
nodes.summary: Formats an entry count with comma thousands separators for the listing log line.

nodes.name: plan_listings
nodes.summary: Derives the auto-merged .dir group listings: groups the [[asset]] ops by dir in first-appearance order, reads the shipped i.dat as the authoritative row table, and rebuilds each allow-listed listing payload from the shipped bytes plus the mods' new names, decoding each host pack once.

nodes.name: plan_one_listing
nodes.summary: Plans one group's .dir listing: finds the shipped row, checks membership and host, slices the shipped listing bytes out of the decoded host pack, and extends them with the contributors' names, refusing loudly and leaving the listing vanilla at every failure.

nodes.name: listing_group
nodes.summary: The membership and host checks for one listing group, returning its contributors, mods and single resolved host; it refuses non-allow-listed listings, an explicit [[asset]] override of the row, and hosts that disagree.

nodes.name: tailgate_site_anchor
nodes.summary: Maps a family-A host pack to its per-pack tailgate splice anchor name (vp, tp, mcp, ep, cp), or None for a host with no tailgate site that must serve through the merge instead.

nodes.name: tailgate_hosts
nodes.summary: Lists the hosts a tailgate decision touches in first-appearance order: every [[asset]] host, then every listing host not already present.

nodes.name: plan_family_a_need
nodes.summary: Computes the largest family-A host requirement the plan implies: each host's vanilla declared size plus every appended asset payload and derived listing payload.

nodes.name: maybe_grow_workspace
nodes.summary: Arms the family-A decode-workspace swap when the plan or an explicit workspace_out_mb asks for more than the shipped buffer, returning the grown size or 0 on refusal so the game's own buffers stay (fail-open).

nodes.name: decide_and_grow
nodes.summary: The two-pass tailgate decision: decide against the workspace the game will allocate, grow the workspace when the plan needs more, re-decide against the grown cap, then record the declared sizes and the tailgated set on the plan.

nodes.name: decide_tailgate
nodes.summary: The tailgate decision entry: short-circuits on an empty asset plan or asset_serving = merge, else delegates to plan_tailgate and converts any abandonment into a merge decision carrying its loud reason.

nodes.name: plan_tailgate
nodes.summary: The tailgate body: gathers the inputs, assembles the per-host ordered item lists and i.dat rows from the shared planner, budget-checks and plans per-host sites, adds the i.dat site, installs the shared cave plus every site, and reports tailgate versus merge per host.

nodes.name: gather_tailgate_inputs
nodes.summary: Gathers the tailgate inputs: per-host vanilla declared sizes, every asset payload read once, the shipped i.dat plus its collision check, and the decode-funnel and relay-cave anchors, carrying the declared sizes read so far on every abandonment.

nodes.name: read_declared_sizes
nodes.summary: Reads every host's and i.dat's vanilla family-A declared size, keeping whatever was read on failure and naming the unreadable file.

nodes.name: read_asset_blobs
nodes.summary: Reads every [[asset]] payload once in resolved order so the tailgate can append from memory without touching the mod dirs again.

nodes.name: check_shipped_collisions
nodes.summary: Refuses an [[asset]] name that exists in the shipped i.dat without override_vanilla, the same authoritative check the merge performs, handing the whole tailgate over to merge.

nodes.name: resolve_funnel_cave
nodes.summary: Resolves the two shared anchors, the family-A decode funnel and the shared relay cave, requiring non-empty expect bytes on each.

nodes.name: build_host_items
nodes.summary: Assembles the per-host ordered item lists (assets then listings, exactly the order overlay::host_ops uses) and the i.dat rows, taking every offset from the shared family-A layout planner so rows and appends cannot disagree.

nodes.name: plan_host_sites
nodes.summary: Per host: budget-checks cap minus declared, resolves the pack's tailgate site anchor and builds a SitePlan; a host that does not fit or lacks a site anchor joins the merge fallback list.

nodes.name: plan_idat_site
nodes.summary: The i.dat site: joins the merge path whenever any host did (atomicity, since the rows are appended before the stage-2 host decodes), when the rows do not fit, or when the build has no i.dat site anchor; otherwise it tailgates with the row-count bump.

nodes.name: install_sites
nodes.summary: Installs the shared relay cave plus every planned site and returns the pack keys actually spliced; a cave install failure is the one fatal outcome and yields an empty set.

nodes.name: loose.rs
nodes.summary: The [[loose_asset]] table: game files the game opens by path are materialized into <mods_dir>/cache/loose/ at install time as real files, and every CFile::Open is matched against the compiled patterns before the pack logic, rewriting the open path to the cache copy on a hit.

nodes.name: merge.rs
nodes.summary: The overlay's merge side: builds the merged pack at most once per run per key (decode original, apply ops, re-encode via a9-formats under a size budget), writes it atomically beside an FNV-1a staleness key, and specialises the csvp table merge, the i.dat master-index merge and the family-A host append.

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: The runtime overlay: one trampoline hook on MFC CFile::Open that normalizes the path, serves matching [[loose_asset]] cache copies, captures pack opens for the injector, and redirects an overlayed pack's open to a loader-managed content-hashed cache, passing every unmatched path and every failure straight to the original open.

nodes.name: LooseEntry
nodes.summary: One materialized [[loose_asset]] redirect: a compiled path pattern plus the loader-cache file whose bytes must be served in its place.

nodes.name: try_serve
nodes.summary: Serves a matching [[loose_asset]] cache copy in place of the normalized path, or None when the table is empty or nothing matches so the caller runs the pack logic.

nodes.name: materialize_loose
nodes.summary: Materializes the [[loose_asset]] cache copies: reads each payload, writes <mods_dir>/cache/loose/<name> (overwritten every boot) and compiles its pattern, dropping any failing asset with one loud line.

nodes.name: unique_loose_name
nodes.summary: Builds the collision-free cache file name <mod-id>__<sanitized pattern>, disambiguating with a counter when two distinct patterns in one mod sanitize to the same string.

nodes.name: sanitize_name
nodes.summary: Maps a string to a cache-name-safe form (keeping [a-z0-9._-], everything else to underscore) and bounds it to 100 characters for the Windows path-component limit.

nodes.name: stat_key
nodes.summary: The (mtime in ns, size) fingerprint of a payload file, or (0,0) when it cannot be read.

nodes.name: ensure_cache
nodes.summary: The hook-facing cache entry: returns a remembered result or builds the merged pack once per run per key, deliberately not holding the built-set lock across the build so the i.dat merge can re-enter for its host packs.

nodes.name: build_cache
nodes.summary: The merge: reads the original pack, returns early when the staleness key still matches, and otherwise merges and writes the cache atomically (tmp plus rename) together with its key file.

nodes.name: cache_fingerprint
nodes.summary: The FNV-1a staleness hash over the pack key and every op's identity, content-addressed for csvp payload bytes and stat-based for the read-at-merge families, so a changed mod set rebuilds and an unchanged one boots from cache.

nodes.name: merge_pack
nodes.summary: Dispatches the merge by key family (the csvp table container, the i.dat master index, a family-B image pack or a family-A asset host) and logs a per-family summary line.

nodes.name: host_ops
nodes.summary: The full ordered payload list for one family-A host: its [[asset]] payloads read from the mod dirs, then its auto-merged .dir listings, the single list both the pack merge and the i.dat rows take their offsets from.

nodes.name: merge_family_a_host
nodes.summary: The family-A host merge: appends the host's asset payloads and its derived listings to the decoded stream (merged = vanilla ++ payloads), re-encodes and budget-checks.

nodes.name: merge_idat
nodes.summary: The master-index merge in load-bearing order: parse the shipped i.dat, refuse shipped-name collisions without override_vanilla, build every referenced host pack's cache first so no row can point past a vanilla image, synthesize rows from the shared planner, then serialize and re-encode.

nodes.name: idat_hosts
nodes.summary: The referenced host list for the i.dat merge, in first-appearance order over assets then listings and deduped.

nodes.name: idat_rows
nodes.summary: Synthesizes the i.dat rows from the same family-A planner the host merges used, taking a tailgated host's base from its boot-time declared size and a merged host's from its decoded length.

nodes.name: Packs
nodes.summary: The runtime op tables the overlay hook consults: family-B image ops per pack, csvp table ops, [[asset]] ops, derived .dir listings, the tailgated set the hook must leave alone, per-host vanilla declared sizes and the materialized loose table.

nodes.name: CsvOpPlan
nodes.summary: One csvp table op handed over by the engine with its payload already read and row overlap refusal already applied.

nodes.name: AssetOpPlan
nodes.summary: One [[asset]] op handed over by the engine: the host family-A pack, the bare i.dat key, the dir field, the owning mod dir, the payload file and the override_vanilla flag.

nodes.name: ListingOpPlan
nodes.summary: One auto-merged .dir group listing the engine derived from the mods' own [[asset]] rows: the host, the listing row key and the already-rebuilt payload.

nodes.name: LooseOpPlan
nodes.summary: One [[loose_asset]] op handed over by the engine: the game path pattern and the mod-relative payload the overlay must materialize and serve in its place.

nodes.name: Plan
nodes.summary: The plan the engine hands to the overlay at boot: image entry ops per pack, csvp table ops, [[asset]] ops, derived listings, the tailgated pack set, per-host declared sizes and the loose ops, consumed by install.

nodes.name: install
nodes.summary: Installs the overlay at boot: hooks cfile_open with an expect-verified trampoline, materializes the [[loose_asset]] cache copies, folds the plan into the runtime op tables and stores the singleton state.

nodes.name: from_plan
nodes.summary: Folds the engine's plan handover into the runtime op tables: image entry ops, csvp table ops, [[asset]] ops, .dir listings, the tailgated set, the per-host declared sizes and the materialized loose table.

nodes.name: my_cfile_open
nodes.summary: The CFile::Open hook: normalizes the path, tries the [[loose_asset]] table, captures the pack identity for the injector, and redirects an overlayed pack's open to its cache path, passing anything unmatched or failing straight to the original open.

nodes.name: path_to_string
nodes.summary: Converts a UTF-16 open path to a normalized String (ASCII-lowercase, forward slashes to backslashes, no leading dot-backslash), refusing null and runaway strings.

nodes.name: pack_key
nodes.summary: Shapes a normalized open path into a pack key: data\<pack>.bin (or a bare name) to the pack name and data\i.dat to i.dat, with None for anything that is not a pack path.

nodes.name: pack_file_name
nodes.summary: The on-disk name for a cache or original key: <key>.bin for packs and the game's own i.dat for the master index.

nodes.name: overlay_key
nodes.summary: Decides whether the pack named by an open is touched by the overlay plan at all: never for a tailgated pack, only for csvp when table ops exist, only for i.dat when asset rows or listings ride it, and otherwise for image packs or family-A asset/listing hosts.

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: Module barrel for the direct spec-row injection subsystem: documents the mechanism in depth and declares the four submodules (spec, train, car, diag), re-exporting TrainRow and install_trains as the seam the engine boot path drives.
nodes.languageNotes: Rust module barrel: submodules declared in dependency order and the public seam re-exported with pub use.

nodes.name: spec.rs
nodes.summary: Resolved engine state, anchor expect-verification and the spec_table_resize hook that grows the game's spec-row vector past its 421-row re-pin and appends a cloned, freshly named reserved row; also the shared row-layout constants both injection paths read.
nodes.languageNotes: Engine functions are typed as Rust fn-pointer aliases and reached through core::mem::transmute of stored RVAs.

nodes.name: train.rs
nodes.summary: The [[train]] path: builds one spec row per compiled mod train from a donor clone, hooks train_list_builder to inject them after the pipeline fills its rows, and applies the 18-lane name-pointer clone fix so the live teardown cannot double-free.
nodes.languageNotes: Hook bodies are extern "system" trampolines that forward to the original via a stored trampoline pointer.

nodes.name: car.rs
nodes.summary: The car build: drives the game's own car-model loader once per declared car so an injected row gets real model objects, model slots and formation data the CSV pipeline can never supply, plus the train_form.csv column to spec-row field mapping.
nodes.languageNotes: Scratch buffers are deliberately leaked (Box::leak) so a game-side overrun lands in loader-owned memory with a checked canary tail.

nodes.name: diag.rs
nodes.summary: Opt-in loader diagnostics shared by both injection paths: a Wine-safe panic-hook replacement, consist copier/creator trampoline probes, and a per-train_list_builder spec-row dump used to observe what the renderer actually resolves.

nodes.name: apply_form_row
nodes.summary: Applies a train's train_form.csv columns to a cloned spec row (cruise and reverse speed, accel, base fare, the four sound ids, preview coordinates, special/mode flags) and forces the row valid, taking only numeric cells and keeping the donor's value for anything else.

nodes.name: build_cars
nodes.summary: Drives the game's own car-model loader per declared car (train_model_fetch, model_register, model_index_alloc) to give an injected row real model slots, then writes the per-car fields and formation block, using leaked canary scratch buffers and failing open to the donor's car data.

nodes.name: capture_panic
nodes.summary: Formats a panic message (payload plus location) into a static slot and emits a fixed banner through OutputDebugStringA, so a loader panic is at least named under Wine where the default backtrace symbolizer dies.

nodes.name: install_panic_capture
nodes.summary: Replaces the default panic hook with capture_panic so a loader panic is reported as a readable message instead of crashing inside the backtrace symbolizer.

nodes.name: my_consist_copy
nodes.summary: Trampoline hook over the consist row copier: logs the form/aux car entries the renderer actually resolves, then runs the original and returns its result unchanged.

nodes.name: install_consist_probe
nodes.summary: Installs the expect-verified consist-copier trampoline and publishes the trampoline address plus the logger to the probe hook.

nodes.name: my_consist_create
nodes.summary: Trampoline hook over the consist object creator: logs the source car-entry list and the object the game creates, then forwards to the original.

nodes.name: install_consist_create
nodes.summary: Installs the expect-verified consist-creator trampoline and publishes its address and logger for the probe hook.

nodes.name: probe_row_map
nodes.summary: Per-train_list_builder diagnostic that dumps the live spec-row map: row validity, resolved names, the reserved ids and the form/aux car entries, so injection results can be compared against vanilla rows.

nodes.name: resolve_entry
nodes.summary: Resolves the running build's address-book entry from the exe's VERSIONINFO build id, refusing when the exe cannot be read or the build is unknown.

nodes.name: anchor_bytes
nodes.summary: Reads len bytes at base plus the anchor RVA after an is_readable check, returning an error instead of crashing on unreadable memory or a missing anchor.

nodes.name: verify_anchor
nodes.summary: Expect-verifies one anchor against the address book's recorded bytes and refuses on any mismatch or missing expect bytes.

nodes.name: ensure
nodes.summary: Prepares the resolved state once: resolves the build, expect-verifies the four spec anchors, publishes the global singleton state, and optionally installs the spec_table_resize trampoline.

nodes.name: inject_now
nodes.summary: The bare reserve primitive: ensures state and runs the locked injection, growing the live spec vector and appending the reserved rows at the current end.

nodes.name: inject_locked
nodes.summary: Core injection with the state lock held: validates the spec vector and template row, builds a cloned row with engine-constructed names in a scratch buffer, grows the vector through the engine's own realloc, and copies the row in.

nodes.name: my_resize
nodes.summary: Trampoline hook over spec_table_resize: runs the original re-pin first and only then injects, so a growth done earlier is not silently undone, and logs the outcome.

nodes.name: a9loader_m7_rows
nodes.summary: Harness export that drives ensure plus inject_now (or reads the reserved row back) outside the boot path so the injection mechanism can be exercised without the game.

nodes.name: TrainRow
nodes.summary: One train to inject: allocated id, FORM and display names, donor FORM name, speeds, fare and car count, the model directory and mesh profile, capacity/running cost/price, and the derived train_form and train_pattern CSV rows.

nodes.name: TrainState
nodes.summary: Immutable install-time state for train injection: resolved engine addresses, the optional annotator-bound and roster-clamp patch sites, the car-build helper addresses, the resolved donor/TrainRow list, the trampoline and boot progress flags.

nodes.name: form_id
nodes.summary: Reads the live FORM name literal and resolves a donor FORM name to its position (id), returning None when the anchor or the name is missing.

nodes.name: install_trains
nodes.summary: Boot entry point for [[train]]: expect-verifies every anchor, resolves each train's donor id and copies its data, installs the train_list_builder trampoline plus the optional annotator-bound and roster-clamp patches, and wires the consist probes and car-build helpers.

nodes.name: my_train_list_builder
nodes.summary: Trampoline hook over train_list_builder: injects the mod rows before the original walks the vector so the keep-set admits them, optionally runs the car build, and forwards to the original.

nodes.name: a9loader_m7_dump
nodes.summary: Harness export that decodes a mod's built pack and prints its CSV tables, so the authoring side of a train can be inspected without booting the game.

nodes.name: inject_trains_locked
nodes.summary: Core multi-row injection: reallocates the spec vector through the engine, clones each donor row, rebuilds all 18 name lanes with the clone-ref fix and fresh formatted names, applies the CSV form row, and widens the annotator and roster clamp patch sites to the live row count.

nodes.name: Cargo.toml
nodes.summary: Cargo manifest for the `a9-mod` crate — the A-Train 9 mod model (manifest schema, dependency resolution, build identity, anchor address book, loader config). Declares a workspace-inherited version/edition/license and depends on `a9-formats` plus serde, semver, toml and thiserror.

nodes.name: builds.toml
nodes.summary: The per-build anchor address book: for game build 5.00.5634 it maps 59 named anchors to an in-image RVA plus the original `expect` bytes (57 anchors carry the byte fingerprint; the two runtime-pointer anchors — workspace_globals and train_spec_manager — carry none). Manifests reference anchor names, never raw RVAs, and every anchored write is expect-verified before it lands so a game update fails loudly instead of corrupting memory. The anchors cover the train-list filter, the family-B injector and family-A LZSS tailgate splices, the decode-workspace swap, the purchase/editor whitelist scans, the save-id clamp guards, the direct spec-row injection and the `[[train]]` pass sites.
nodes.languageNotes: Heavily commented TOML: each `[build."<id>".anchors.<name>]` table is documented in place with the disassembly it fingerprints, the PE file offset (file = rva - 0xC00 for .text/.rdata) and the ABI/alignment reasoning behind the hook boundary.

nodes.name: dirindex.toml
nodes.summary: The per-build `dir → host pack` index for game build 5.00.5634, generated by `a9ml gen-dirindex` from a live install: 1300 dir mappings in `dirs`, 49 exact-name rescues in `names`, and 25 ambiguous dirs in `ambiguous` (dirs whose rows span packs, which `host = "auto"` refuses). Recovered empirically by testing every shipped i.dat row against every decoded pack buffer, it answers which pack is resident when an asset's consumers run.
nodes.languageNotes: A large generated TOML keyed by build id with three sibling tables; keys with backslashes are single-quoted (literal) strings, and `ambiguous` values are inline string arrays.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Index of the mod-developer documentation tree: links every guide page (getting started, manifest, memory/content effects, loader config, layout, tooling, diagnostics, limits) and states the core rules in one screen — a mod is a folder with mod.toml, install is a folder copy, the game directory stays vanilla, only Steam build 5.00.5634 is supported, and every effect is validated before execution.

nodes.name: content-effects.md
nodes.summary: Reference for the data-stage (non-address-touching) effects — [[pack]] family-B image entries, [[csv]] csvp tables in replace/rows mode, [[asset]] new family-A i.dat rows with auto host resolution, [[loose_asset]] path-matched file serving — plus the retired [[file]] effect, auto-merged .dir listings, serving modes (inject/merge, tailgate/merge) and family-A workspace capacity limits.
nodes.languageNotes: Written as field tables per TOML section (field/type/required/notes) with explicit validation and refusal rules for each effect.

nodes.name: diagnostics.md
nodes.summary: Explains the loader log format and verbosity, the per-boot lines written (banner, plan, patch journal, merge decisions, closing count), the optional probes, and the fail-open philosophy — every failure (build mismatch, byte mismatch, unreadable RVA, oversized host, failed cache build) refuses the write and serves vanilla instead of corrupting memory; also tabulates conflict/overlap outcomes and the cache/journal locations.

nodes.name: folder-layout.md
nodes.summary: Describes the on-disk shape of a mod folder (mods/<id>/mod.toml plus entries/, csv/, assets/ and hook side files), the path-resolution rules (mod-relative, slash-normalised, the no-absolute/no-drive/no-.. check applying only to [[loose_asset]].file and [[asset]].folder) and the folder→name/dir derivation plus name-uniqueness rules.

nodes.name: getting-started.md
nodes.summary: Five-step install guide for the version.dll proxy (drop it next to ATrain9v5.exe, WINEDLLOVERRIDES on Wine/Proton, create mods/, one folder per mod), the minimal valid mod.toml, build compatibility via game_builds, and the boot-time order of execution (config read → scan/build-id gate → resolve → memory stage → data stage → runtime stage).

nodes.name: limits.md
nodes.summary: Explicit list of what v1 deliberately does not support ([native]/code mods, scripting sandboxes, signature anchors, before/after ordering, per-mod stores, content bundles, FORM slots past 417, in-image _a0_* sign assets, unproven .dir auto-merge, second builds, GUI) together with the real bounds of the supported features (workspace sizes, the full 24-row family-B pool, tailgate refusals, new trains vs saves, loose-asset re-materialisation, enabled=false).

nodes.name: loader-config.md
nodes.summary: Reference for a9loader.toml next to the exe: the lenient parse policy (missing file = silent defaults, unknown keys and bad values warn rather than fail), every key with type/default/meaning (log_level, mods_dir, allow_conflicts, disabled, enabled, the diagnostic probes, pack_serving, asset_serving, workspace_out_mb) and the [order] table for sequence and per-mod priority overrides.

nodes.name: memory-effects.md
nodes.summary: Reference for the two memory-stage effects: [[patch]] (raw bytes at an anchor+offset, expect-verified, VirtualProtect → verify → write → restore → FlushInstructionCache, journaled) and [[hook]] (built-in handlers train_list with allow/add/deny list composition into one bitmap, and nop), plus the named anchors a mod may target and the loader-owned seams it must not.

nodes.name: mod-manifest.md
nodes.summary: Specification of mod.toml: the strict deny_unknown_fields schema, required and optional root fields (id/name/version/author, game_builds, priority, supplies/requires/conflicts), the dependency and conflict resolution semantics and order, a table of every effect section ([[patch]], [[hook]], [[pack]], [[csv]], [[asset]], [[loose_asset]]) with the retired [[file]], the TargetRef forms, and a full example manifest.

nodes.name: tooling.md
nodes.summary: Guide to the optional a9ml authoring/diagnostic CLI: the command table for mod authors (list, doctor, classify, extract-csv/patch-csv, extract-asset/merge-assets, diff-pack, diff-csv, mkpack, gen-dirindex), the optional format-check commands (verify, inspect), and the edit-loop notes including the loader-maintainer step of regenerating the embedded dirindex after adding a new dir.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Documents the Wine test harness: the fake-game host, the shared helper library, prerequisites, and a per-milestone table mapping each script to the host modes it drives.

nodes.name: lib.sh
nodes.summary: Shared helper library sourced by every harness: scenario assembly (new_scen), the Wine host runner (run_host), grep-based assertions backed by a shared fail counter, and fixture/payload helpers.

nodes.name: m2.sh
nodes.summary: Engine harness proving the full loader under Wine against a fake-game host: config parsing, the build gate (right/wrong VERSIONINFO), mods scan and resolve, expect-verified patch/hook execution and the train_list filter modes, asserting both end effects and the loader log.

nodes.name: m3.sh
nodes.summary: Runtime-overlay harness exercising the CFile::Open trampoline under Wine: expect verification, hook install, redirect into the loader-managed pack cache and passthrough, with byte-exact content checks against a9ml-built packs.

nodes.name: m4inj.sh
nodes.summary: Inject harness for pack_serving = "inject": splices the famb pool-runner call site, appends an in-memory row over the vanilla slice, and checks the missing-payload refusal plus register/byte discipline.

nodes.name: m4probe.sh
nodes.summary: Fetch-probe harness: maps the four fetch anchors and asserts the probe install/per-call log lines when enabled and their absence when disabled, plus the purchase-window tabfix, custom-form formfix, window dump and clamp-guard probe pages.

nodes.name: m5.sh
nodes.summary: [[asset]] harness: appends payloads to a family-A pack's decoded stream and verifies the merged i.dat rows byte-exactly, covering the folder/auto dir-index form and the no-shipped-row and ambiguous-dir refusals.

nodes.name: m6.sh
nodes.summary: [[loose_asset]] harness: game files opened by path served from a loader-managed cache copy via case-insensitive glob matching, covering absolute/relative/exact paths, no-match passthrough, unreadable-payload fail-open and two-mods overlap.

nodes.name: m7rows.sh
nodes.summary: Spec-row-injection harness: drives the a9loader_m7_rows export to grow the 421-row spec table to 422 through the resize hook, and checks the name-ctor and template-name refusals plus the pre-resize wrong-order hazard.

nodes.name: m7train.sh
nodes.summary: [[train]] compiler harness: runs the loader's real boot scan against a fake host to compile a train and install the keep-set with reserved ids, the overlay plan and the injection hook, then verifies the four derived csvp rows byte-exactly and the refusals.

nodes.name: run-all.sh
nodes.summary: Gate runner: executes every harness/m*.sh in name order, logs each to harness/run/all.log, prints per-harness verdicts, and exits non-zero when any script is not green.

nodes.name: check
nodes.summary: Asserts a needle is present in a file via grep and increments the shared fail counter when it is missing.

nodes.name: checkf
nodes.summary: Runs a command and records pass/fail into the shared fail counter, suppressing its output.

nodes.name: checkq
nodes.summary: Asserts a needle is ABSENT from a file, failing the scenario when it appears.

nodes.name: mod
nodes.summary: Creates a mod directory under the current scenario and writes its mod.toml manifest from the supplied body lines.

nodes.name: pay
nodes.summary: Copies a prepared payload file into a mod's tree at the given relative path.

nodes.name: py_mk
nodes.summary: Writes a deterministic ramp-byte payload of a given size and seed through an inline Python one-liner.

nodes.name: run_host
nodes.summary: Runs the fake host under Wine inside the scenario directory with a 60-second timeout, capturing output so a crashed host fails fast instead of hanging the debugger.

nodes.name: new_scen
nodes.summary: Assembles a fresh scenario directory: copies the host exe, the loader DLL, the FORM list and the optional default config, then invokes the sourcing script's scen_fixtures hook.

nodes.name: harness_done
nodes.summary: Prints the harness verdict and exits with the accumulated failure count, emitting the ALL SCENARIOS GREEN marker on success.

nodes.name: mk_csv
nodes.summary: Writes a UTF-16 BOM CSV with CRLF line endings and every field quoted — the game's own table style — from pipe-separated row arguments.

nodes.name: trainlist_mod
nodes.summary: Emits a train_list-filter mod fixture for the probe scenario, wiring the filter hook target and its mode.

nodes.name: tg_fixtures
nodes.summary: Builds the canned vanilla decoded streams and the expected merged images used by the family-A asset scenarios.

nodes.name: m5u_tp_fixtures
nodes.summary: Builds the preview fixture — a real previewtexture.dir inside the tp pack plus its payloads — for the vp preview scenarios.

nodes.name: m5u_tail_expect
nodes.summary: Asserts the merged vp pack's tail listing against the expected payload names for the preview scenarios.

nodes.name: mk_csv
nodes.summary: Writes a UTF-16 CSV fake table from pipe-separated rows for the [[train]] derived-row byte comparison.

nodes.name: Cargo.toml
nodes.summary: Workspace manifest declaring the four member crates (a9-formats, a9-loader, a9-mod, a9ml) and the shared package metadata inherited by all of them: version 0.1.0, edition 2024, CC0-1.0 license.
nodes.languageNotes: Cargo workspace with resolver 3; members inherit metadata via `version.workspace` / `edition.workspace` / `license.workspace`.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Project front page for a9loader: what the in-memory mod loader does, the supported Steam build, the workspace layout, build/install steps, the full mod.toml effect reference (hook/patch/pack/csv/asset), and the test and tooling matrix.

nodes.name: Cargo.toml
nodes.summary: Manifest for the a9-formats codec crate; declares its three dependencies (flate2, md-5, thiserror) and inherits the workspace package metadata.

nodes.name: Cargo.toml
nodes.summary: Manifest for the a9-loader DLL product: depends on a9-formats/a9-mod/toml, sets `[lib] name = "version"` so cargo emits version.dll, and gates the opt-in probe diagnostics behind the default `probe` feature.
nodes.languageNotes: The cdylib lib name is deliberately `version` so the artifact is version.dll; an rlib is also built so `cargo test` links the crate cleanly.

nodes.name: Cargo.toml
nodes.summary: Manifest for the a9ml authoring/diagnostics CLI: depends on the a9-formats and a9-mod crates plus anyhow, clap (derive), flate2, semver and toml.

nodes.name: tests.rs
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the [[train]] compiler: id allocation and naming, the four derived csvp rows, the documented effect-key set, and every refusal mode (all offline, no game involved).

nodes.name: host.c
nodes.summary: The fake game host for every Wine harness (m2..m7train): maps fake pages at the real RVAs carrying the real original bytes so expect-verified patch/hook installation passes, loads the built version.dll, and drives the fake call sites per mode string.
nodes.languageNotes: Heavily uses inline __asm__ undo thunks to replay the game's real prologues and hand control to plain C bodies, and __attribute__((used, noinline)) so the compiler cannot eliminate bodies referenced only from asm.

nodes.name: host.rc
nodes.summary: VERSIONINFO resource stamping the M2 harness host with the international Steam build id 5,0,0,5634 so the loader's build gate accepts the fake host.

nodes.name: host_wrong.rc
nodes.summary: VERSIONINFO resource stamping a WRONG-build host (5,0,0,9999) used to prove the engine refuses all memory effects with a loud log line and boots vanilla.

nodes.name: sec
nodes.summary: Test helper that builds a TrainSection with the given key/name and every optional field set to None.

nodes.name: allocation_and_naming
nodes.summary: Asserts a train's derived FORM name, icon stem, id allocation and defaulted name_en, and that a mod's second train receives the next id.

nodes.name: derived_train_form_row_is_exact
nodes.summary: Parses the compiled train_form payload and asserts the derived row matches the expected shape column-for-column.

nodes.name: derived_pattern_group_is_a_10_row_group_plus_separator
nodes.summary: Asserts the compiled train_pattern payload is a 10-row group followed by a separator row.

nodes.name: derived_comment_and_custom_rows
nodes.summary: Asserts the compiled train_comment and train_custom payloads carry the expected derived rows.

nodes.name: declarations_override_the_defaults
nodes.summary: Asserts that a train's declared overrides (names, form, model, livery, ...) replace the derived defaults in the compiled output.

nodes.name: effect_keys_are_the_documented_set
nodes.summary: Asserts the compiled train's effect-key set equals the documented csv/asset/hook/train keys.

nodes.name: refusals_skip_only_the_bad_train
nodes.summary: Asserts each refusal mode (path traversal, missing/odd model names, spaces, ...) skips only the offending train and leaves the good ones compiled.

nodes.name: range_exhaustion_refuses_loudly
nodes.summary: Asserts that exceeding the reserved id range refuses loudly and reports the overflow rather than wrapping.

nodes.name: compile_all_threads_ids_across_mods
nodes.summary: Asserts compile_all allocates ids across multiple mods in order without collision.

nodes.name: cfile_open_body
nodes.summary: Fake MFC CFile::Open body: records the path the open actually used (the redirect evidence), opens it with CreateFileW, and fills the CFile layout (+8 handle, +0x10 valid flag).

nodes.name: fake_runner_body
nodes.summary: Fake famb pool-runner stand-in (the injector's spliced call target): dumps the pool's worker rows (start, entry count, mode byte, array) and returns the sentinel 0x4711.

nodes.name: tg_decode_body
nodes.summary: Fake family-A LZSS decoder: copies a canned decoded stream into dest, reproduces the live decoder's tail overrun, and writes the produced length back to *cap.

nodes.name: ws_setup
nodes.summary: Builds the fake workspace-swap environment: the singleton's game buffers and caps, the alloc-tail site bytes, the pinned callee, the CC cave, and trampolines to the fake _aligned_malloc/_aligned_free bodies.

nodes.name: setup_filter_pages
nodes.summary: Maps the filter-fn and whitelist/FORM data pages and writes the recorded original filter prologue plus the two whitelist table entries the address book expects.

nodes.name: setup_cfile_page
nodes.summary: Maps the fake CFile::Open page with its 16-byte original prologue and patches an E9 tail jump into the undo thunk after mapping.

nodes.name: setup_probe_pages
nodes.summary: Maps the four fetch-probe fake pages (pack/tex/ccom/cache), laying each anchor's expect bytes, the chkstk completion for the two alloca sites, and its undo thunk.

nodes.name: tab_body
nodes.summary: Fake type-tab rebuild body: replicates the patched rebuild — valid row + composed membership through the relay cave + tab-type match — and appends matching ids to +0x48.

nodes.name: setup_tab_pages
nodes.summary: Maps the window/row fix-up fake pages (tab rebuild + scan, relay cave, window, manager), lays their expect bytes and undo thunks, and writes the custom-train-form scan's two branch markers.

nodes.name: mgr_setup
nodes.summary: Builds the fake spec-table manager: 400 valid type-0 rows, the three index vectors, and a pre-seeded composed keep-set at +0x48 (ids 4/16/42 whitelisted, 329 not).

nodes.name: setup_save_pages
nodes.summary: Lays the four save-side mmf helper prologues + E9 undo tails and builds four in-image caller stubs so the probe's logged caller RVA is deterministic.

nodes.name: setup_clamp_pages
nodes.summary: Maps the always-on save-id clamp pages (head site, head cave, car site + cave) and installs the fake mmf_paged_read shim that the car site's E8 targets.

nodes.name: rows_realloc_body
nodes.summary: Fake spec-vector reallocate: allocates a new block, copies the live rows, sets {begin,end,cap}, and re-points the accessor's base — the game-allocator stand-in.

nodes.name: rows_make_template
nodes.summary: Builds the shipped valid template row (row 0): bValid=1, one car, JP/EN/form names, a clone marker, and two extra non-NULL lanes so the clone fix has something to clone.

nodes.name: setup_rows_pages
nodes.summary: Maps the rows ctor page, plants the accessor plus the three called helpers (resize/realloc/ctor) with undo thunks, allocates the 421-row fake spec table, and repoints the manager's rows vector at it.

nodes.name: form_id_of
nodes.summary: Locates a FORM name's index in the mapped comma-separated UTF-16 FORM list (trimming surrounding whitespace), returning -1 when the name is absent.

nodes.name: fake_fetch_body
nodes.summary: Fake train_model_fetch: reports the wrapper's capacity/running/price and the 17 pattern-row cells, stores a non-NULL car object in the wrapper, and returns success.

nodes.name: setup_train_pages
nodes.summary: Maps the train-injection fake pages: the tlb/clone-ref sites with undo thunks, the rcstr prologue call redirect, the four car-build helpers with completing bytes, the 0x400000 ret block, and the annotator bound.

nodes.name: setup_tailgate_pages
nodes.summary: Plants the family-A decode shim and the vp/tp/i.dat call sites' E8 expect bytes with a ret continuation, and points the workspace out at the tailgate out buffer.

nodes.name: setup_workspace_pages
nodes.summary: Writes the fake workspace environment before the DLL loads, and for the combined tailgate-ws mode hands the singleton the tailgate's workspace out buffer.

nodes.name: setup_inject_pages
nodes.summary: Maps the inject fake pages (spliced site, fake runner, pool, capacity, workspace/stream, caves, malloc/free fakes), plants the famb site bytes and runner shim, and builds the 2-entry fake decoded family-B stream.

nodes.name: mode_overlaypackcsv
nodes.summary: Merge-scene game: opens data/mtfake.bin or data/csvp.bin through the (possibly hooked) CFile::Open, reads it whole, and reports which path the open used and its size.

nodes.name: mode_overlaydat
nodes.summary: The [[asset]] scene: opens data/i.dat (stage 1) and data/vp.bin (stage 2) through the hooked CFile::Open and reports each path and byte size.

nodes.name: mode_overlaytp
nodes.summary: The .dir merge scene: opens data/i.dat (the host-cache stage) then data/tp.bin through the hooked CFile::Open, reporting path and size.

nodes.name: mode_loose
nodes.summary: [[loose_asset]] scene: opens an absolute glob-matching path, an exact relative path and a non-matching path through the hooked CFile::Open, dumping the bytes read for an offline compare.

nodes.name: mode_probe
nodes.summary: Runs all four fetch-probe anchors once through their (possibly hooked) entries so the loader's probe logs its four lines; without the probe installed the fakes run instead.

nodes.name: mode_tabfix
nodes.summary: Tab-fix evidence: calls the composed-keep relay cave directly with a set of ids and reads back the patched scan site's bytes.

nodes.name: mode_formfix
nodes.summary: Form-fix evidence: calls the composed-keep cave for several ids and runs the rewritten custom-train-form scan end-to-end to read its keep/drop branch decision.

nodes.name: mode_window
nodes.summary: Window probe evidence: calls the (possibly hooked) window and tab-rebuild entries and shrinks +0x48 between calls so the diagnostic's delta line fires.

nodes.name: mode_save
nodes.summary: Save-path probe evidence: calls the four (possibly hooked) save-side mmf helpers through in-image caller stubs so the probe logs caller RVA + size, the two block lines and the read-side line.

nodes.name: mode_clamp
nodes.summary: Clamp evidence: calls the head site with in/out-of-range ids and the car site over a mixed 0xf8 block (including slot-0 repairs), reading the clamped ids and slots back.

nodes.name: mode_rows
nodes.summary: Direct spec-row injection evidence: maps the rows pages and drives the a9loader_m7_rows export through each scenario (rows/order/refuse/refuse-tmpl/off), reading the injected row through the game's own accessor and walking the live vector.

nodes.name: train_populate_donor
nodes.summary: Marks the FORM_AR4 donor row valid with the lane shape the clone fix exercises (JP/EN/form names, extra lanes, and a formation block the car build must not touch).

nodes.name: mode_train
nodes.summary: The [[train]] host path: fires the train_list_builder injection hook (with an optional retry phase), reads the injected row and consist through the game's accessor, prints the composed-filter verdict, and opens csvp.bin so the overlay merges the derived rows.

nodes.name: mode_inject
nodes.summary: Inject scenario host path: opens the pack (the capture seam), fills the fake pool the way the vanilla refill leaves it, then calls the spliced site plain (rax forwarding) and under the EBX sentinel.

nodes.name: mode_tailgate
nodes.summary: Tailgate scenario host path: feeds the i.dat and vp decode sites a fake in-buffer plus canned vanilla decoded bytes, then dumps the post-decode workspace for a byte-exact compare.

nodes.name: mode_tailgate_tp
nodes.summary: The tp-host tailgate variant: feeds the i.dat site then the tp site with canned decoded bytes and dumps enough of the tail for several appended payloads and a listing.

nodes.name: mode_workspace
nodes.summary: Workspace-swap evidence: calls the spliced alloc-tail site and reports the callee rax, the malloc request size, the out swap and the cap raise; workspace-fail makes the allocator return NULL.

nodes.name: mode_nop
nodes.summary: Identity check for the filter hook: calls the filter fn with a small array and asserts it returns its out pointer and that the new-end pointer equals end.

nodes.name: mode_filter
nodes.summary: Calls the (possibly patched) train-list filter with 1024 sequential ids and prints how many were kept and whether ret == out.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Harness entry: maps every fake page the address book expects, loads the built version.dll, sanity-checks a forwarded export, copies the real FORM list into its mapped region, and dispatches on the mode string to one handler per scenario family.

nodes.name: encode_pack_b
nodes.summary: Encodes a family-B pack body: LZSS-encode the decoded bytes and wrap them with the MD5-header cipher (bare entry-table family, no declared-size prefix).

nodes.name: from_field
nodes.summary: Wraps a raw 0x200-byte name field straight into a NameField without decoding, so the padding bytes after the NUL survive the parse verbatim.

nodes.name: field
nodes.summary: Returns the raw 0x200-byte field for serialization — the verbatim counterpart of the decoded as_str view, which is what keeps re-encoding byte-identical on real packs.

nodes.name: header_matches
nodes.summary: Checks the file's 16-byte header against MD5 of the plaintext body — the game's own integrity check — and returns false for anything shorter than the header.

nodes.name: key
nodes.summary: Returns the row's first column as its identity key for the row-merge tier, or an empty string when the row has no columns or the first is empty.

nodes.name: raw
nodes.summary: Returns the row's exact UTF-16LE content bytes without its line terminator, the verbatim half that makes parse to serialize byte-identical.

nodes.name: eol
nodes.summary: Returns the row's line terminator variant (CRLF, LF, CR, or none for a final row with no newline), kept per row so serialization reproduces the original bytes.

nodes.name: push_row
nodes.summary: Appends a row encoded canonically (every field quoted, UTF-16LE, CRLF terminator) — the authoring path used when writing patch tables.

nodes.name: len
nodes.summary: Returns the number of rows in the table, counting header and comment rows as well as data rows.

nodes.name: is_empty
nodes.summary: Reports whether the table holds no rows at all.

nodes.name: column_count
nodes.summary: Returns the field count of the table's first row (the header the author supplied), the reference width every patched or appended row is checked against; 0 for an empty table.

nodes.name: retain_rows
nodes.summary: Drops rows the predicate rejects, used by the loader to enforce per-row overlap refusal before the merge runs.

nodes.name: v1
nodes.summary: Reads the first u32 of an entry's verbatim 9-byte tail — the byte length consumers get for the row (for a .x, including its 12-byte ADX0 chunk header).

nodes.name: v2
nodes.summary: Reads the single flag byte at tail offset 4 — zero in every shipped row.

nodes.name: v3
nodes.summary: Reads the u32 the loader takes unaligned at tail offset 5 — the row's offset into the current pack's decoded buffer.

nodes.name: row
nodes.summary: Looks up the master-index entry with this bare name, returning None when the index has no such row.

nodes.name: plan_family_a
nodes.summary: Returns the (offset, length) each asset payload lands at when appended to a family-A stream, off_i = |V| + the sum of earlier payload lengths; the single layout source both the host-pack merge and the i.dat row writer must call.

nodes.name: family_a_total
nodes.summary: The decoded size of the merged family-A image (vanilla length plus the sum of all payload lengths), the value the merge declares as the new pack's output size.

nodes.name: family_a_fits
nodes.summary: Whether the merged family-A image stays within the engine's decode workspace cap, the check the tailgate runs against the 200 MB output budget to choose tailgate over merge per host pack.

nodes.name: listing_auto_merge
nodes.summary: Whether a .dir group listing is on the auto-merge allow-list — the deliberately narrow set of listings whose consumers provably match entries by exact name, so the append position cannot matter.

nodes.name: classify_key
nodes.summary: The normalization the pack classifier matches on: the lowercased basename with any .bin suffix stripped.

nodes.name: parse_allow_list
nodes.summary: Parses an allow-list text file into a list of FORM names: one name per line, trimmed of spaces/tabs/CR, dropping blank lines and `#`-comment lines. Matching against the FORM list happens later in build_bitmap and is exact and case-sensitive.

nodes.name: BitmapReport
nodes.summary: Result of build_bitmap: the FORMS_MAX-bit keep bitmap plus the counts of allow-list names that matched a FORM entry and those that matched nothing (unmatched names are ignored, exactly like the C reference).

nodes.name: composed_allowed
nodes.summary: Returns the composed train_list keep-bitmap installed for this boot, or None when no mod declared a train_list contribution (the game's own 97-entry whitelist then applies). The tab-rebuild and custom-form-readout fixes re-derive list membership from exactly this set.

nodes.name: composed_kept
nodes.summary: Tests whether the installed composed keep-set admits a spec-row id; None when no composed filter was installed. Used by the harness seam a9loader_m7_kept to assert that reserved [[train]] ids are admitted.

nodes.name: Contribution
nodes.summary: One mod's train_list contribution: mod id, list mode, list-file name, matched/unmatched counts, the resolved hook RVA with its expect bytes, and the per-form keep bitmap. Contributions are parsed at boot and composed into a single filter instead of letting one mod own it.

nodes.name: InjectOp
nodes.summary: One inject operation handed from the engine to the famb splice: mod id and version, entry name, width/height, mod directory and payload file. It mirrors the overlay's PendingImageOp but carries no cache-address fields — payloads stay raw decoded bytes.

nodes.name: InjectorPlan
nodes.summary: The inject mode's plan: pack name (as the manifest spells it) mapped to the ops to append, in priority order — overlap losers are already refused by the resolver. The engine fills it from resolved pack image effects and consumes it in injector::install.

nodes.name: is_empty
nodes.summary: True when the plan carries no pack entries; the engine then skips install_inject entirely, so no famb splice is installed and the game's vanilla pack loading stays untouched.

nodes.name: line
nodes.summary: Appends an untagged informational line to the loader log with a local HH:MM:SS timestamp; it never panics and never fails the boot.

nodes.name: debug
nodes.summary: Appends a `DBG:  `-tagged line; the overlay gates these calls on the config's log_level=debug, so the emitter itself does not check the flag.

nodes.name: warn
nodes.summary: Appends a `WARN: `-tagged line for non-fatal problems (e.g. a declined optional effect) while the boot continues.

nodes.name: err
nodes.summary: Appends an `ERR:  `-tagged line for failures that trigger the loader's fail-open paths; like every log call it is total and never fails the boot.

nodes.name: as_ptr
nodes.summary: Returns a Trampoline's thunk entry address so a hook can call the saved original function with the original's signature. The thunk is allocated once at boot and never freed, so the pointer stays valid for the process lifetime.

nodes.name: Spec
nodes.summary: One resolved probe anchor handed over by the engine: the builds.toml anchor name, its RVA and the recorded expect bytes. probe::install trampolines the anchor at that RVA after verifying the expect bytes, forwarding every call verbatim to the original.

nodes.name: MEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION
nodes.summary: Win32 MEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION (x64 layout, including the PartitionId WORD) as filled by VirtualQuery. sys::is_readable inspects its State and Protect fields to decide whether a range is committed and safe to read.

nodes.name: SYSTEMTIME
nodes.summary: Win32 SYSTEMTIME filled by GetLocalTime; log.rs reads wHour/wMinute/wSecond from it to stamp each log line.

nodes.name: DisableThreadLibraryCalls
nodes.summary: Raw Win32 FFI declaration: at DLL_PROCESS_ATTACH the loader tells Windows the proxy needs no per-thread attach/detach notifications, avoiding needless loader-lock callbacks.

nodes.name: GetModuleHandleW
nodes.summary: Raw Win32 FFI declaration: resolves a module handle by name — the loader uses it to find the host process's own module by full system path.

nodes.name: LoadLibraryW
nodes.summary: Raw Win32 FFI declaration: loads a module by full path; forward.rs uses it to load the real version.dll lazily (never inside DllMain) before resolving its exports.

nodes.name: GetProcAddress
nodes.summary: Raw Win32 FFI declaration: resolves an exported symbol address from a module handle, used by forward.rs to obtain the real DLL's exports to forward the proxy's own exports to.

nodes.name: GetSystemDirectoryW
nodes.summary: Raw Win32 FFI declaration: writes the Windows system directory into a UTF-16 buffer; forward.rs uses it to build the full path of the real system DLL to forward to.

nodes.name: VirtualProtect
nodes.summary: Raw Win32 FFI declaration: changes page protection and reports the previous protection; patch::write_bytes calls it before every code/data write so hook sites can be made writable.

nodes.name: FlushInstructionCache
nodes.summary: Raw Win32 FFI declaration: flushes the CPU instruction cache after code bytes are written, so a freshly installed hook or trampoline is actually executed.

nodes.name: GetCurrentProcess
nodes.summary: Raw Win32 FFI declaration: returns the pseudo-handle to the current process, passed as the process argument of FlushInstructionCache.

nodes.name: VirtualQuery
nodes.summary: Raw Win32 FFI declaration: fills a MEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION for an address; it is the primitive behind sys::is_readable, which guards raw-RVA manifest targets so a typo refuses instead of crashing the game.

nodes.name: GetLocalTime
nodes.summary: Raw Win32 FFI declaration: fills the current local SYSTEMTIME; it is the source of the HH:MM:SS timestamp on every loader log line.

nodes.name: VirtualAlloc
nodes.summary: Raw Win32 FFI declaration: commits/reserves pages. The loader allocates its executable trampoline thunks and the injector's pinned per-pack extension region with it (MEM_COMMIT|MEM_RESERVE, PAGE_READWRITE).

nodes.name: VirtualFree
nodes.summary: Raw Win32 FFI declaration: releases or decommits an allocation; patch::install_trampoline frees a failed thunk allocation with MEM_RELEASE. The injector's extension region deliberately is never freed.

layers.name: Format Codec Library
layers.description: Byte-exact A-Train 9 file-format codecs — the pack cipher and ADD table, LZSS, family-A/family-B containers, i.dat, savegame carving, CSV tables, and the overlay merge engine that the loader and the CLI share deliberately.

layers.name: Mod Model & Resolution
layers.description: The a9-mod mod model: manifest schema and validation, dependency/conflict resolution, mods-directory scanning, loose-asset globbing, build-identity gating, the pure train compiler, and the embedded anchor/dir-index table accessors.

layers.name: Loader Bootstrap & Platform Primitives
layers.description: The version.dll proxy itself and its low-level platform layer — lazy export forwarding, Win32 FFI, expect-verified patch codegen, the game-allocator workspace, one-line logging, FORM-name reading, and the reverse-engineering probe hooks.

layers.name: Effect Planning Engine
layers.description: The loader's boot engine: turning a resolved mod set into an ordered effect plan, refusing any anchor that fails expect-verification, planning tailgate asset serving, and emitting the boot report.

layers.name: In-Memory Effects
layers.description: The effects the loader applies inside the running game — the save clamp guard, the CFile::Open overlay redirect for loose and merged packs, family-A/famb injection, tab and form readout fixes, and the spec-row/train/car row-injection subsystem.

layers.name: Authoring & Diagnostics CLI
layers.description: The a9ml binary: verify/inspect/list/doctor/classify boot analysis, pack and asset authoring (mkpack, extract/merge assets, CSV patching), train and manifest dry runs, pack diffing, self-tests, and the gen-builds/gen-dirindex regenerators for the embedded tables.

layers.name: Wine Test Harness
layers.description: The Wine-only test harness that needs neither the game nor an install: the fake game host (host.c with RVA-mapped pages and build-id resources), the shared lib.sh helpers, and the per-milestone scenario scripts driven by run-all.sh.

layers.name: Documentation
layers.description: The project front page and the docs/ tree: getting started, folder layout, mod manifest, loader config, memory and content effects, diagnostics, tooling, limits, plus the harness README.

layers.name: Workspace Configuration & Generated Tables
layers.description: Non-code declarative inputs: the workspace and per-crate Cargo manifests, the generated-but-hand-extended builds.toml anchor address book and dirindex.toml, and the analysis ignore list.

tour.title: What a9loader Is
tour.description: The front page states the project's one-sentence contract: it is a mod loader for A-Train 9 v5, a Rust workspace whose effects all execute at boot inside the game process through a version.dll proxy, so installing a mod is copying its folder and the game directory stays vanilla. It also names the supported build (international Steam 5.00 / build 5634) and the four crates that the rest of this tour walks through. Read it first — every later step is a piece of this contract being honoured.

tour.title: Workspace and Crate Boundaries
tour.description: The workspace manifest declares the four member crates and the package metadata they share, and each crate manifest fixes that crate's dependency direction: a9-formats depends on almost nothing, a9-mod depends only on formats, a9-loader and a9ml both sit on top of those two. That shape is deliberate — the format codecs are the single source of truth, shared by the loader and the tooling, exactly so a second implementation cannot drift. These eight files are the cheapest map of the whole system.
tour.languageLesson: In a Cargo workspace, `[workspace.dependencies]` plus `dep.workspace = true` keeps one version per dependency across all members, so the codecs the loader links are literally the same release the CLI links. Separate crates also make the dependency direction a compile-time fact rather than a convention: a9-formats physically cannot import a9-loader.

tour.title: The Format Codec Foundation
tour.description: Everything downstream assumes these codecs are byte-exact against the shipped game data, so the crate root simply declares them and the shared Error type. crypt.rs holds the pack cipher — an MD5(plaintext) 16-byte header that doubles as the XOR key plus the ADD-table keystream; add.rs is the 256-byte ADD table transcribed from the exe and cross-checked against shipped packs; lzss.rs is the decompressor that matches the game's loader at 0x140314bf0 with read-as-you-write back-references, and a greedy encoder proven byte-identical to the reference packer; pack.rs wraps both in the family-A/family-B framing. This layer is what makes 'the game directory stays vanilla' possible: the loader serves mods by decoding and re-encoding in memory instead of ever writing a file.
tour.languageLesson: The read-as-you-write back-reference loop is why this decoder cannot be swapped for a generic LZSS crate: the specs disagree about whether overlapping copies observe already-emitted bytes. Encoding is likewise specified as an algorithm (greedy, 22-bit hash chain) rather than a format, so byte-identity requires the same tie-breaking, not just a valid stream.

tour.title: Containers, i.dat, and the Merge Engine
tour.description: Above the raw codecs sit the container shapes and the operations the tooling and the overlay both perform on them. container.rs handles the family-B entry tables, including the 0x200 UTF-16 name field that must be preserved verbatim because shipped packs carry garbage in the padding. idat.rs parses and rewrites the i.dat master asset index, and the overlay/ modules implement the three merge shapes — replace/append an image entry, patch or append csvp rows, and append family-A payloads — each returning a MergeReport. Because these are the same routines the loader calls at boot and a9ml calls offline, a mod author can dry-run exactly what the loader will do.

tour.title: The Mod Model: Manifest, Scan, Resolution
tour.description: A mod is data, and the a9-mod crate is what makes that data mean something. manifest/mod.rs defines the strict mod.toml schema, sections.rs gives serde shapes to every content-adding section ([[patch]], [[hook]], [[pack]], [[csv]], [[asset]], [[loose_asset]], [[train]]), and validate.rs checks each section before it is ever trusted. scan/mod.rs finds every <mods_dir>/<mod>/mod.toml, parses and validates it, expands asset folders and reads the mod's own train CSVs, skipping broken mods loudly; resolve/mod.rs then turns the manifests plus config knobs into the execution order, the skips with reasons, and the effect-overlap report. Both the loader and the CLI consume that one plan, which is how 'what the CLI told you' and 'what boot did' stay the same thing.

tour.title: Build Identity and the Anchor Address Book
tour.description: The loader refuses to patch on a mismatch, and this is the machinery that decides what 'match' means. buildid.rs reads the game exe's PE VERSIONINFO straight from the file bytes — no Win32 API, so there is no loader-lock hazard — and yields the canonical id such as 5.00.5634. builds.rs loads the anchor address book builds.toml, which maps 59 named anchors to an in-image RVA plus the original expect bytes the loader must verify before any anchored write; dirindex.rs loads dirindex.toml, the empirically recovered dir-to-host-pack table that resolves host = "auto" assets. Supporting a new game build means adding entries to these two files, not changing any mod.
tour.languageLesson: builds.toml is generated but hand-extended: `a9ml gen-builds --check` owns the core anchor set and catches drift, while RE-discovered anchors are appended by hand. Treating a generated file as also editable only works when a `--check` mode exists to catch someone hand-editing the generated half — a pattern worth copying in any tool that emits a checked-in artifact.

tour.title: The DLL Product Entry
tour.description: This is the artifact users actually deploy: a cdylib whose lib name is `version`, so cargo emits version.dll, dropped next to ATrain9v5.exe. lib.rs declares the mostly Windows-only loader modules and owns DllMain, which boots the engine on DLL_PROCESS_ATTACH and always returns 1 so the game can never be blocked from starting. forward.rs supplies the 10 VERSION.dll exports the proxy must provide and forwards them to the real system DLL, loading it lazily on the first forwarded call so nothing runs inside DllMain under the loader lock. Steps 3-6 supplied the codecs and the plan; here they get a process to run in.
tour.languageLesson: A proxy DLL works because Windows resolves imports by name and file, so a version.dll earlier in the search order interposes; the loader must still export every symbol the exe imports or startup fails. Doing the real-DLL load lazily instead of in DllMain avoids the loader-lock deadlock that would otherwise hang the process on its own first forwarded call.

tour.title: Platform Primitives: FFI, Patches, Workspace, Log
tour.description: Four small modules carry all the low-level risk. sys.rs is the hand-declared Win32 surface plus the two readability guards that turn a typo'd RVA into a loud refusal instead of an access violation. patch.rs is the x86-64 splice machinery: VirtualProtect/write/restore/flush writers, the `jmp [rip+0]` relay cave that lets a same-image E8 reach a stub many GB away, E8 rel32 splicing with pinned original targets, and the prologue-relocating trampoline installer. workspace.rs raises the family-A decode ceiling by swapping the 200 MB output buffer for one allocated with the game's own allocator, and log.rs writes the one-line-per-event a9loader.log that never panics and never fails a boot. Expect-verification and fail-open are not policies in one place — they are built out of these primitives.
tour.languageLesson: Rust here is `unsafe` FFI plus raw memory writes, and the crate's discipline is to keep the unsafety in narrow, auditable modules and to return a Result for anything that could be wrong (bad RVA, unexpected bytes) rather than letting it become UB. Foreign allocations must also come from the game's allocator — a block from Rust's allocator would crash the game's own teardown.

tour.title: The Boot Engine and the Effect Plan
tour.description: engine/mod.rs is the whole boot sequence in one function: read config, identify the running build from the exe, scan and resolve mods, apply expect-verified patches and hooks, then plan and install the overlay, tailgate, injector and train-row injection before logging the final applied/refused count. plan.rs folds [[pack]], [[csv]], [[asset]], [[loose_asset]] and [[train]] sections into either the overlay serving plan or the injector plan, applying per-effect overlap refusal as it goes, while tailgate_plan.rs derives the auto-merged listings and decides — per host — whether family-A payloads can simply be appended in place at the decode instead of going through the merge path. report.rs emits the end-of-run line that states the game continues, which is the visible half of fail-open.

tour.title: Applying Effects Inside the Game
tour.description: These are the effects themselves. handlers.rs holds the executors for [[patch]] and [[hook]] — including the train_list filter, the only loader code that runs inside the game's own call path — with every write expect-verified and every failure a logged Err. injector.rs implements pack_serving = "inject": the mod's decoded image blocks are appended straight into the family-B loader's worker-row pool the game's loader threads consume, so there is no re-encode, no cache file, nothing on disk. tailgate.rs does the same trick for family-A by splicing the game's single LZSS decode funnel and appending mod bytes into the shared decoded workspace, and clamp.rs is the always-on save-id guard that bounds saved formation ids to the live spec-table row count so an old save degrades instead of reading past the heap block.

tour.title: The CFile::Open Overlay Redirect
tour.description: Not every effect can be an in-memory splice, so the loader also owns the game's one file-open funnel: MFC CFile::Open. overlay/mod.rs installs a single trampoline hook that normalizes the path, serves matching [[loose_asset]] cache copies, captures pack opens for the injector, and redirects an overlayed pack's open to a loader-managed content-hashed cache — passing every unmatched path and every failure straight to the original open. overlay/loose.rs materializes path-opened game files into <mods_dir>/cache/loose/ at install time and matches them case- and slash-insensitively, and overlay/merge.rs builds a merged pack at most once per run, writing it atomically beside an FNV-1a staleness key. This is the fallback tier: the inject and tailgate paths in Step 10 exist to avoid needing it.

tour.title: Row Injection and the Train Compiler
tour.description: Adding a train is the hardest case, because no CSV table can reach a row past the game's fixed 417-entry per-form index arrays — so the runtime data must be materialised by the loader. a9-mod/src/train.rs is the pure compiler: it turns a declared [[train]] into an allocated spec id and FORM name, four derived csvp rows, three preview icons and the effect keys. On the loader side, rowinject/mod.rs documents the mechanism, spec.rs owns the spec_table_resize hook that grows the game's spec-row vector past its 421-row re-pin and appends a cloned, freshly named reserved row, train.rs builds one row per compiled train and applies the 18-lane name-pointer clone fix so the live teardown cannot double-free, and car.rs drives the game's own car-model loader once per declared car to get real model objects and formation data. This is where the project's most expensive reverse-engineering lives.

tour.title: The a9ml Authoring CLI
tour.description: a9ml is never required to run a mod and nothing it does gets installed, but it is how everything in this project is proven. main.rs is the user-visible contract: the clap argument model holding every subcommand's names, flags and defaults. verify.rs proves the format library against real packs (self-tests, then decrypt/decode/container-invariant/round-trip/rebuild-parity sweeps, optionally differential against the C oracle), mkpack.rs builds and byte-verifies a pack, classify.rs answers the practical question of whether a texture replace actually reaches the game by naming the boot stage that consumes each effect, and gen_builds.rs regenerates builds.toml from a live exe with provenance — with --check acting as the update-day drift gate from Step 6.

tour.title: The Wine Test Harness
tour.description: The project's gates cannot depend on the game being installed, so harness/host.c is a fake game host that maps fake pages at the real RVAs carrying the real original bytes — enough for expect-verified patch and hook installation to pass — loads the built version.dll, and then drives the fake call sites according to a mode string. lib.sh is the shared helper library every scenario sources (scenario assembly, the Wine host runner, grep-backed assertions with a shared fail counter), run-all.sh runs every harness/m*.sh in order and exits non-zero if any is not green, and m7train.sh is the worked example: it runs the loader's real boot scan against the fake host and verifies the four derived csvp rows byte-exactly. In a project where a mistake crashes the game, this is what makes iteration cheap.
tour.languageLesson: The host fakes the game by mapping pages at the addresses the loader will patch, so the harness exercises the real patch codegen without Wine needing to run the exe. That is the general trick for testing a program that must attack another process's memory: reproduce the target's memory image and build identity, then assert on the attacker's journaled decisions.

tour.title: Documentation: The Contract and the Limits
tour.description: The docs/ tree is where the loader's guarantees are stated for mod authors, and it is deliberately explicit about both what works and what does not. docs/README.md indexes the pages; getting-started.md gives the five-step install and the boot-time order of execution (config read, build-id gate, resolve, memory stage, data stage, runtime stage) that Step 9 implements; memory-effects.md and content-effects.md are the references for the two effect families from Steps 10-11. limits.md is the most valuable page: it names what v1 refuses — code mods, signature anchors, FORM slots past 417, second builds — alongside the real bounds of what is supported. Read it as the honest counterpart to the README's promise.
